verification.summary:
NOVELTY / PRIOR-ART LENS on docs/methods/BDG_HANDOFF.md.

HEADLINE: no citation in §8 is fabricated — all four exist and three of four characterisations are accurate. But the one citation that is mis-described (MGD) is precisely the one that occupies BDG's headline ownership claim, and of the four items in §8's "what is ours", one is refuted by a test I ran, one is refuted by this repo's own code, one is a restatement of a comment already in proj1/src/guidance.py, and one is occupied by a literature §8 does not cite at all (closed-loop / feedback guidance scale).

WHAT I VERIFIED BY RUNNING CODE (scratchpad/bdg/openloop_replay.py, CPU numpy toy, no generator loaded):
1. §3's affine factorisation holds: max |(y-F_i) - eta*e*(F_i-Fbar) - w_eff*(y_eff-F_i)| = 7.1e-15 over 2000 draws. The handoff is right about its own reduction.
2. The repo's OWN prior spec (Three_New_Guidance §5.2, nu* = R C^T (C R C^T)^-1 b) is ALSO affine in F_i, to 1.8e-15. So the §3 reduction does not distinguish BDG from the one-sided proposal §8 says it improves on — both are "plug reweighted".
3. §8's claim (d), "the loop does not reduce to any fixed weight schedule", is FALSE as literally written. Replaying the realised time-varying (w_eff(t), y_eff(t)) open-loop reproduces the closed loop to 4.2e-17 (tighten) and 5.6e-17 (widen). For a deterministic sampler such a schedule always exists. Worse, a CONSTANT mean weight recovered sd/unguided to within 2.7% and 0.5% in my toy — so the handoff's reported catastrophic constant-weight failure (2.53x vs 1.17x) is a regime fact, not a structural one, and its control confounds three changes at once (drops time-variation, drops the y_eff shift, drops the feedback). The salvageable claim is TRANSFER: replaying the schedule on a different batch missed by 17% / 5%.
4. In the widen branch the controller runs at w_eff in [-2.087, +0.488]. BDG's widening IS negative/sub-unit guidance weight at a shifted target — which is the handoff's own open item #2, where plain plug at negative w already beats BDG on alpha.

RATINGS of §8 "what is ours": (a) two-sided narrow+widen = KNOWN (MGD). (b) stability argument = INCREMENTAL, already written in this repo's guidance.py. (c) scale-free setpoint-relative error = KNOWN, and V/tau^2 is already a repo diagnostic. (d) not-a-fixed-schedule = REFUTED as written; the transfer version is INCREMENTAL and occupied by Feedback Guidance (2506.06085).

"Batch-feedback-adaptive guidance weight" as a CLASS is known. The specific instance (weight driven by the batch variance of a predicted scalar property against a setpoint) I could not find published verbatim in a bounded search — call it narrow and unclaimed, not novelty-cleared.

PROBABILITIES: (i) slightly novel for a course project 0.85 (I agree with the handoff's 0.85); (ii) workshop 0.05 (handoff says 0.1 — I am lower, because the two claims a workshop reviewer would test first, (a) and (d), are the two that fail); (iii) main conference 0.01. Biggest single lever for (ii): drop the controller framing and ship the impossibility result (coverage is sigma-governed; tightening breaks the chemistry floor, widening lowers coverage by definition) with negative-weight plug as the headline comparator.

PLACEMENT: docs/methods/ is the right directory, but BDG is absent from GUIDANCE_METHODS_INDEX.md and from INNOVATION_IDEAS_INDEX.md §3.2's four-criteria novelty table; every other arm has a row in both. No bdg code or results exist in the main tree (only inside another session's worktree), so every §6/§7 number is unverifiable from here.

findings.claim: §8: "moment correction (MGD, arXiv 2602.17211)"; §3: "spbc/MGD's mean-only corrector"
findings.evidence: arXiv 2602.17211 exists and is real: Lempereur, Cuvelle-Magar, Coeurdoux, Mallat, Vanden-Eijnden, "MGD: Moment Guided Diffusion for Maximum Entropy Generation", submitted 19 Feb 2026, revised 6 Sep 2026. But it is NOT mean-only and NOT a mere "correction". From the HTML: the SDE (Eq. 13) dX_t = (eta_t^T - sigma^2 theta_t^T) grad phi(X_t) dt + sqrt(2 sigma) dW_t; the corrector (Eq. 25) solves h sigma^2 G'_k theta_k = (1/n_rep) sum_i phi(y_k^i) - m_(k+1) h, i.e. the drift coefficient is set by the residual between the EMPIRICAL ENSEMBLE moment and a TARGET moment m_t. That residual is sign-free, so the correction is two-sided. The paper emphasises quadratic moment functions phi(x) = (x_i x_j)_{i<=j} capturing covariance (Theorem 4.1 proves exact solutions for this case). So MGD is already a two-sided, empirical-ensemble-vs-setpoint controller on second moments. That is exactly §8's headline ownership claim (a), "removing the positive-part restriction so one controller both narrows and widens". Describing it as mean-only makes the closest prior art look distant.

findings.claim: §8's four citations exist and say what the handoff says they say
findings.evidence: No fabricated citations — all four resolve. Particle Guidance = arXiv 2310.13102, Corso, Xu, De Bortoli, Barzilay, Jaakkola, ICLR 2024; repulsive joint-particle potential, no setpoint: characterisation HOLDS. Variance-Tilted Diffusion = arXiv 2606.22239, Azangulov, Zhang, Ashouritaklimi, submitted 20 Jun 2026; Doob h-transform of independent diffusions, "prescribed linear feature map", "favours collections of samples with large empirical spread", interaction term repelling posterior denoised means + curvature term toward higher feature variance, no target value: the handoff's "monotone, can only widen, on a fixed linear feature" is EXACTLY right. MMD Guidance = arXiv 2601.08379, Mahdizadeh Sani, Jamali, Jalali, Farnia, submitted 13 Jan 2026, revised 9 Jun 2026; gradients of MMD between generated samples and a reference dataset: "divergence-to-a-reference matching" HOLDS. Only MGD is mis-described (separate finding). Note VTD's "repels posterior denoised means" is structurally BDG's widening branch, which §8 does not acknowledge.

findings.claim: §3 / §8(d): "Freezing w_eff at its time-average and running plain plug at that constant weight fails to reproduce BDG... A fixed schedule cannot do that" / "the demonstration that the resulting loop does not reduce to any fixed weight schedule"
findings.evidence: I built a deterministic batch toy (B=64, D=6, nonlinear property f(x)=sum(Wf*tanh(x)), 60 steps, eta=4) that reproduces BDG's update algebra, ran the closed loop, recorded the realised (w_eff(t), y_eff(t)), then replayed it OPEN-LOOP. Result: max|F_open - F_bdg| = 4.163e-17 (tighten, tau=0.6x) and 5.551e-17 (widen, tau=1.5x). A fixed time-varying schedule reproduces the loop bit-for-bit — as it must for any deterministic sampler. Further, a CONSTANT mean weight was close, not catastrophic: sd/unguided 0.7033 vs BDG's 0.7230 (tighten) and 1.0662 vs 1.0714 (widen), despite w_eff ranging over [1.054, 18.799] and [-2.087, 0.488]. And the handoff's control is confounded: "plain plug at that constant weight" changes THREE things at once (kills time-variation, kills the feedback, and drops the y_eff target shift, since plain plug aims at y). Separating them in my toy, constant-w-with-y_eff (0.7033) and constant-w-with-original-y (0.7046) differ by 0.2%, so in my regime the shift is not the driver — but the control as run cannot establish that. The one version that does hold up is TRANSFER: replaying the realised schedule on a DIFFERENT batch gave sd 0.149098 vs the closed loop's 0.127140 on that batch (17% miss, tighten) and 0.221007 vs 0.210404 (5% miss, widen). That is the claim the paper should make, and it is a different claim.

findings.claim: §8: the repo's own §5.2 one-sided controller is the prior art, and what is ours is "removing the positive-part restriction" — implying the §3 reduction is a property that separates BDG from it
findings.evidence: I solved §5.2's allocation nu* = R C^T (C R C^T)^-1 b numerically over 500 random draws (B=64, C_1i=1/B, C_2i=2c_i/B, R=diag(r_i)) and checked it against r_i*(lambda_1/B + 2*lambda_2*c_i/B): max deviation 1.776e-15. So §5.2's per-sample coefficient is ALSO affine in F_i (mobility-weighted), hence also "plug reweighted" under §3's own general statement ("any guidance whose per-sample coefficient is affine in F_i is plug reweighted"). Reading §5.2 directly: it already uses V = batch variance of the terminal property FORECAST z_i (i.e. BDG's V_b, not btvg's V_F), already has the setpoint tau, already derives Delta V = (2/B) sum_i c_i nu_i (the same signed-deviation gradient BDG derives in §2), and §5.3 already writes the closed-loop ODE Vdot = -k_V (V - tau^2)_+. The ONLY delta from the team's own already-written spec is deleting (.)_+ and swapping the least-squares allocation for a scalar gain. A reviewer who reads the repo's own docs will land here first.

findings.claim: §8(c): "the setpoint-relative scale-free error e" is ours
findings.evidence: e = (V_b - tau^2)/tau^2 = V_b/tau^2 - 1. This repo's btvg2 arm ALREADY persists exactly that ratio as a diagnostic: proj1/src/guidance.py:785, "btvg2_V_over_tau2": (V / tau2).detach(). Normalising an error by its setpoint is also textbook proportional control — CFG-Ctrl (arXiv 2603.03281) states outright that classifier-free guidance "is mathematically equivalent to a proportional state-feedback controller acting on semantic alignment error, where the guidance scale serves as the proportional gain". This is the weakest of the four ownership claims and should be dropped rather than defended.

findings.claim: §8(b): "the stability argument that licenses removing it (the clamp is only necessary for the vanishing per-sample V_F, not for V_b)" is ours
findings.evidence: The argument is CORRECT and the repo's code confirms its premise — but the premise is already written down in this repo, in the comment block guarding the clamp. proj1/src/guidance.py (the btvg_var branch, ~lines 1478-1494) already says: "V_F is a per-sample posterior variance and goes to 0 as t -> 1 by construction (k = (1-t)^2/t falls by ~780x over t in [0.5, 0.975]), while tau^2 is a population band half-width. So V_F < tau^2 eventually happens on EVERY trajectory regardless of the batch, and without this clamp the sign flip turns the last ~15% of every run into active widening (measured b = +5.3, +110.8, +78.6)." BDG's contribution is the contrapositive of an argument already in the tree, plus the empirical observation that V_b does not vanish. Useful and true; not new material. Note also that stability analysis of a guidance controller is itself occupied — CFG-Ctrl provides "Lyapunov stability analysis to theoretically support finite-time convergence".

findings.claim: §8's "Not new" list is a complete map of the prior art that threatens BDG (it lists adaptive guidance scales only as "autoguidance, CFG++, guidance intervals")
findings.evidence: The literature that actually occupies claims (b) and (d) — closed-loop, state-dependent guidance scale — is not cited at all. Three hits, none in the handoff and none anywhere in docs/methods/: (1) "Feedback Guidance of Diffusion Models", arXiv 2506.06085 (Koulischer, Handke et al.) — explicitly frames CFG and friends as OPEN-LOOP controllers "since the guidance scale is not a function of the current state", derives a trajectory-specific state-dependent coefficient that self-regulates, and "challenges the view of guidance as a fixed hyperparameter". That is BDG's framing, pre-empted. (2) "Adaptive Diffusion Guidance via Stochastic Optimal Control", arXiv 2505.19367 — casts guidance scheduling as adaptive optimal control with strength selected from time, current sample and condition. (3) "CFG-Ctrl: Control-Based Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance", arXiv 2603.03281 — CFG as P-control with fixed gain, replaced by sliding-mode control with Lyapunov stability. Citing only autoguidance/CFG++/intervals makes the adaptive-scale category look like scheduling heuristics when it is in fact an explicit control-theory literature.

findings.claim: §8 surveys the prior art relevant to controlling a property's spread
findings.evidence: §8 omits four items THIS REPO had already logged, in tables written before the handoff: TOCFlow arXiv 2601.09474 (terminal/global statistical constraints), Jeffrey guidance arXiv 2606.13240 (prescribed marginal shaping — I verified the abstract: "leverages Jeffrey's rule of conditioning to update marginal distributions towards a prescribed target", training-free; a prescribed property marginal subsumes a prescribed property variance in both directions), Histogram-constrained Image Generation arXiv 2606.31683 (OT distributional constraints during sampling), Multilevel/SMC guidance arXiv 2601.21104. Three_New_Guidance_Ideas_Variance_and_Switching.md:510 already states: "Moment matching itself is occupied by Moment Guided Diffusion. Batch variance interactions are occupied by Variance-Tilted Diffusion... These works rule out broad claims such as 'the first guidance that controls variance.'" Two further items neither the handoff nor the repo lists, which I found: "Controlling Ensemble Variance in Diffusion Models" arXiv 2501.14822 (Merizzi, Evangelista, Loukos) — explicitly aligns ensemble variance to a reference ensemble's spread, bidirectionally, though the mechanism is DDIM step count rather than a guidance term; and CADS arXiv 2310.17347 (condition annealing as a diversity knob, no setpoint). One useful distinction the repo already drew and the handoff drops: PROPOSALS_VARIANCE_TARGETED_GUIDANCE.md:255 records that MMD Guidance "does not target the variance of a scalar observable" — that IS a real gap BDG sits in, and §8 fails to use it.

findings.claim: Is "batch-feedback-adaptive guidance weight" (what §3 says BDG actually is) itself known?
findings.evidence: As a CLASS: yes, twice over. State-dependent/closed-loop guidance scale is Feedback Guidance (2506.06085), Adaptive Guidance via SOC (2505.19367), CFG-Ctrl (2603.03281). Guidance coefficients driven by EMPIRICAL BATCH/ENSEMBLE statistics is MGD (ensemble moment residual vs target sets the drift coefficient) and VTD (interaction term over the batch). The intersection — a scalar guidance weight set by the batch variance of a learned scalar property predictor measured against a setpoint — I did not find published verbatim across ~8 targeted searches. So the honest rating is NARROW and UNCLAIMED rather than new: every ingredient is published, the specific composition was not surfaced. "Not found" here means a bounded search surfaced nothing, not priority.

findings.claim: §8(a): "removing the positive-part restriction so one controller both narrows and widens" is ours; §1: widening is something "no existing arm here can do reproducibly"
findings.evidence: The within-repo half is fine — no other arm here widens reproducibly, and the 1.010x figure from the 1,766-cell scan supports it. The NOVELTY half does not survive: MGD already does two-sided moment control against a setpoint, including quadratic moments (verified above). And my toy shows what the widening branch mechanically IS: in the tau=1.5 run w_eff ranged over [-2.087, +0.488], so widening is nothing but negative / sub-unit guidance weight aimed at a shifted target. That is the handoff's own open item #2, where it already reports plain plug at negative w beating BDG on alpha (1.153x at mol_stab 0.397 vs BDG's 1.034 / 0.373). A reviewer asked to believe "a controller that can widen" will immediately ask why the scalar negative weight is not the paper. Rate (a) incremental, not new; and promote the negative-weight baseline to a headline comparator rather than an open item.
findings.refs: docs/methods/BDG_HANDOFF.md:256-257 (§8), :276-278 (open item 2), :203-206 (§6.1); scratchpad/bdg/openloop_replay.py (WIDEN block, w_eff range)

findings.claim: §8: "Two independent checks rated this yes / yes / marginal with ~0.85 confidence of clearing a 'slightly novel' bar for a course project, ~0.1 for a workshop paper."
findings.evidence: No artifact of those two checks exists anywhere in this repository — grep for BDG/bdg across docs/ returns only BDG_HANDOFF.md itself, and there is no audit JSON, no review doc, no cell. The number cannot be traced, reproduced or scoped (what was searched, by whom, at what depth). Every other novelty claim in this project carries a search-scope statement — e.g. INNOVATION_IDEAS_INDEX.md:346 names which papers were read in full vs at abstract level vs search-summary only, and dates the searches. The handoff should either attach those two checks or drop the figure. My own numbers below are independent of it.

findings.claim: Calibrated probabilities that BDG clears each bar, vs the handoff's ~0.85 / ~0.1
findings.evidence: (i) Slightly novel for a course project: 0.85 — I AGREE with the handoff. It is implemented, gated (28 equivariance checks at 8.7e-19, autograd match 2.8e-14, eta=0 bit-identical to plug), replicated on two seeds, monotone on 6/6 curves, and it self-refutes in §3. Biggest single lever: state the Three_New §5.2 precedent and the §3 reduction in the paper's own voice AND fix the MGD description — the rubric rewards an investigated non-improvement (§4.3, §4.7), so honesty about occupied ground costs nothing and a grader finding it unstated costs a lot. Second lever: the eta=1 seed-2 replication (open item 1, 6 cells ~1 h), since the only cells that beat plug while clearing the floor are eta=1, seed-1 maxima over ~13 cells — the same grid-search artifact that already produced two false results in this project. (ii) Workshop: 0.05, BELOW the handoff's 0.1. Reason: the two claims a reviewer tests first are (a) and (d), and both fail — (a) to MGD, (d) to a 4e-17 open-loop replay. Add n=512, 2 seeds, one backbone, CPU-vs-GPU numerics, and a target the handoff never even states. Biggest single lever: stop selling the controller and sell the impossibility result — coverage is sigma-governed (delta/sigma 0.056-0.169), tightening enough to matter breaks the chemistry floor, widening lowers coverage by definition, therefore NO spread knob on this axis can help. That is a crisp, general, measured negative, and it is the part of this work that is actually not in the literature. Pair it with negative-weight plug as the comparator and replace claim (d) with the cross-batch transfer experiment. (iii) Main conference: 0.01. Lever: the handoff's own §3 tells you the price of entry — a nonlinear function of F_i, or a direction other than g_i — plus at least two backbones and a target protocol matching the project's q90 headline.

findings.claim: Placement and integration of the handoff in this repo
findings.evidence: docs/methods/ is the right directory — all 15 method docs live there and the file is already at docs/methods/BDG_HANDOFF.md (untracked per git status). Two integration gaps: (1) docs/methods/GUIDANCE_METHODS_INDEX.md, whose own column legend says the proof column is "the document with its derivation. Cite this in the paper", has rows for plug, tmpd, tfg_mc, lgd_mc, osc, smg, smg2, smg2_curv, spbc, btvg, btvg_mean, btvg_var, band, rch, kappa3_skew — and no BDG row; (2) INNOVATION_IDEAS_INDEX.md §3.2's four-criteria novelty table (exact match / formula changed / modality differs / base model differs) has rows for A, B, C, D, TRE, BPS, SMG, PCG, RHO, CX, YIELD — and no BDG row. Given §8 makes ownership claims, BDG belongs in that table most of all. (3) No bdg code or results exist in the main tree: grep across *.py/*.json/*.slurm/*.sh finds bdg only inside another session's worktree at .claude/worktrees/wf_bc7c0f18-844-2/, and results/ has no bdg or bdg_seed2 directory. So every number in §6 and §7 is unverifiable from this repo and rests entirely on the other member's Betty tree.

verification.summary:
VERDICT (doability / reasonableness / fit lens, read-only; nothing in the repo was modified).

BDG is valid, well-engineered and honestly self-audited: I independently reproduced its two load-bearing math claims (reduction exact to 1.8e-15; dV_b/dF_i = 2/(B-1)(F_i-F_bar) confirmed by finite differences) and confirmed its §3.6 transfer argument on a simplex toy. It is *not* innovative enough to carry §3.5/§4.4 as the paper's headline, and it cannot be merged into the headline tables: its target is never stated (its plug w=4 control fits q50 at |z|<=0.67 and dist at |z|<=1.11 on 6 metrics, but is 3.1 sigma from q90 on mu), its floor constant is a results/sweep number it forbids using and is 0.03 too strict for its own seed 2, and its n=512 numbers carry ~1 sigma error bars where it claims wins (eta=1 vs plug: +1.38 and +1.04 sigma, maxima over ~13 cells, against the project's own z>=3 rule).

The framing is the weakest part and is target-dependent in a way the handoff never says. On 15,000 real unguided samples I measured: at q50 the batch is nearly centred (bias/delta +2.19/-0.76/-0.88) and spread is the whole lever (tightening buys +0.233/+0.379/+0.428 in_band, debiasing +0.004/-0.002/+0.005) — BDG is aimed at exactly the right lever there. At the project's q90 headline the bias is 9.6-20.5 delta and the entire spread lever is worth +0.0052/+0.0008/+0.0014, with the optimum on the WIDENING side (s*=1.2/1.4/1.1), while debiasing buys +0.048/+0.024/+0.051. So "widening lowers coverage by definition" is false at q90, and "spread control" is a q50-only capability for this project's metric. The repo's own results/btvg3_widening_sim.json already says the same thing (widen_helps true, +0.0019..+0.0069 vs debias +0.025..+0.032). Under `dist` the recast also fails: scaling batch spread buys <=+0.013 unguided and +0.0004 at plug w=4 (s*=1.00); the binding quantity is corr(F,y) (0.13-0.59 -> 0.68-0.80), which no batch-variance setpoint can touch. There is no distribution-matching metric in evaluate_samples, and guided arms already have HIGHER diversity than unguided, so "restore diversity" is not a live need either.

RECOMMENDED PLAN (total ~8-10 person-hours, 0 GPU-hours; CPU partition genoa-std-mem does not compete with the queued 35-62 GPU-h tuned chain). Do NOT make BDG the §3.5 innovation, do NOT re-run it at n=5000x3, do NOT add it to the tuned chain (it would need local delta, batch 128, GPU).
A. Zero-compute repairs, all from cells already on disk (2.0 h, Bobo): A1 state the target and report the BDG tree's own unguided in_band per property (0.25 h — also a free pipeline-agreement check against results/sweep); A2 recompute the floor per seed from BDG's own unguided control instead of 0.362109375 (0.5 h — expected to flip the gap/seed-2 verdict); A3 add bias/delta and sd/delta (and decoded) columns to every cell (0.75 h — this is what decides whether the widening is at fixed centring, the actual capability claim, which is currently unreported); A4 replace bdg_table.py:34's se_prop and print the real z's (0.5 h).
B. Cheap CPU runs (~3 h wall, ~1.5 h attended): B1 eta=1 on seed 2, 6 cells (keep — the handoff's own top item); B2 the matched-spread plug control — plug at the constant w (including negative) that reproduces BDG's achieved sd ratio at equal chemistry, 8-12 cells. B2 is the ablation the template's "matched hyperparameter controls" actually asks for and the one that decides §3's "does not reduce to a fixed schedule"; B3 optional: BDG + controls at q90, 9-18 cells, with the registered prediction from my counterfactual (+0.001 to +0.005 in_band).
C. Artifact port, code only, no re-runs (2-3 h): branch, apply +65/+16/+120, resolve the guidance_sweep.py conflict against b00f11d (--stage tune/tuned_full, --delta-json), run test_bdg.py plus the three regression suites, delete the three *.bak_bdg files. Needed for the 0.525 code points if BDG is cited at all.
D. Placement (1 h): split the single file by the repo's own conventions (methods / protocol / script-generated results / status) and add the GUIDANCE_METHODS_INDEX.md row — BDG currently appears nowhere in this repo except its own handoff.
E. Paper use (1-2 h writing): §4.3 (the guidance-does-not-improve investigation the rubric explicitly rewards — and which this project's own v2 decoded verdict makes live), §4.7 failure mode, §5 mechanism, §3.6/§4.6 transfer (BDG transfers where BTVG's Sigma cannot), appendix table. If time collapses, cut to A1+A2+A3+E (~3 h).

findings.claim: §10: '§3.5 (0.625 pt)' and '§4.4 (0.675 pt, largest Results item)'
findings.evidence: Assignment p.2: '3.5 Proposed Innovation (.625 pt) This is the main Methods subsection.' Results items sum to 2.9 = 4.1 .4 + 4.2 .45 + 4.3 .325 + 4.4 .675 + 4.5 .45 + 4.6 .4 + 4.7 .2, so .675 is indeed the largest single Results item. Defence adds 2c .475 (introduce the innovation) + 2d .45 (test it, of which .3 is the §4.4 table).

findings.claim: §10: '§4.3 — guidance works; the rubric explicitly rewards investigating a non-improvement'
findings.evidence: The clause exists but is narrower than quoted: 'If the target property/condition does not improve from unconditional, investigate the reason and discuss your findings' (assignment §4.3, .325 pt) is about the GUIDANCE-vs-unconditional comparison, not about an innovation that fails. No rubric line rewards an innovation null in the .675 §4.4 slot; credit for a null lives in §4.7 (.2), Discussion (.1) and defence 3d (.1). Separately, the handoff's premise 'guidance works' contradicts this repo's own v2 verdict: on the decoded metric V4 requires, among floor-clearing arms, best-vs-unguided z is mu tfg +2.67 (fails), alpha tmpd +3.57 (clears), gap plug +2.94 (fails). So the non-improvement clause is genuinely live for this project at q90 — which makes BDG's bias-vs-spread decomposition the single best-fitting use of it.

findings.claim: §3.5 fit: BDG is 'a batch-feedback-adaptive guidance weight, not a variance controller' (handoff §3) — does that clear the assignment's innovation bar?
findings.evidence: It clears it structurally: the template lists 'A new guidance mechanism' and sampler/sampling-policy changes as acceptable directions. But the excluded list is one sentence away — assignment §3.5: 'Ordinary hyperparameter tuning, more epochs, more compute, a different random seed, or simply replacing a standard backbone with a larger standard backbone does not count by itself'; template p.6 adds 'performing a larger hyperparameter sweep' and 'simply adding a standard guidance method exactly as published'. A method that provably equals plug at a rescaled weight and shifted target is defensible ONLY through the closed-loop/open-loop contrast, so that control carries the whole §3.5 score — and the handoff's version of it is the weak one (see the §7-vs-§9.2 finding).

findings.claim: §3 reduction: 'num_i is affine in F_i, so it factors exactly ... verified numerically to 1e-14' and 'any guidance whose per-sample coefficient is affine in F_i is plug reweighted'
findings.evidence: Reimplemented from the spec in numpy, B=512, eta=4, tau=1.1: max|num - w_eff(y_eff - F)| = 1.78e-15 (w_eff 3.3002, y_eff 3.5180, e +0.5751). Generalisation: an arbitrary affine numerator a+bF reduces with max err 8.88e-16. Counterexample: a nonlinear numerator sign(y-F)sqrt|y-F| leaves residual 1.394 after the best affine fit, i.e. it is not a reweighting — so the handoff's 'you need a nonlinear function of F_i, or a direction other than g_i' is correct.

findings.claim: §2: 'dV_b/dF_i = 2/(B-1)(F_i - F_bar)', i.e. the dispersion term is the gradient of the batch variance
findings.evidence: Central finite differences on Var(F, ddof=1) over 8 coordinates: max|fd - analytic| = 6.9e-11 against values ~4.1e-3 (relative 1.7e-8, consistent with h=1e-6 truncation). Confirms the term is the exact gradient and that the 2/(B-1) factor is absorbable into eta.

findings.claim: §10/§3.6: 'V_b is the batch variance of a scalar and carries no geometry, so only f_A and the pullback change. Verify this claim before relying on it — it has not been tested on the simplex.'
findings.evidence: Simplex toy (B=512, 40 positions x 8 categories, sum-zero tangent projection): the BDG step is a per-sample SCALAR multiple of the plug step (max within-sample spread of the ratio 1.8e-8, i.e. floating point) and both stay sum-zero (max |row sum| 7e-15 / 5.7e-14). So wherever plug's pullback is valid BDG's is too — no Sigma, no matrix inverse, unlike BTVG's V_F = g'Sigma g whose Sigma = diag(p) - pp' is singular by construction on the simplex (status doc §10). The residual simplex risk (non-negativity, an inequality constraint) is plug's problem, not BDG's. This is BDG's strongest rubric fit: §3.6 (.2) + §4.6 (.4) + defence 3a (.3) — the sections where the project's other variance method structurally cannot go.
findings.refs: scratchpad/bdg/reduction_check.py; docs/status/SCOPE_FM_GUIDANCE_STATUS.md §10 'the simplex transfer is the largest open risk'

findings.claim: The handoff never states which target BDG ran at (coordinator: 'most likely q50')
findings.evidence: Two-sample binomial z (n=512 each) of BDG's plug w=4 control (.1309/.0684/.1602 in_band, .2930/.3438/.2812 mol_stab) against results/sweep plug w=4 tmin0.5: vs q50 |z| <= 0.67 on all six comparisons; vs q90 mu is +3.10 (in_band) and +2.87 (stability). But the v1 dist full run's plug w=4 (n=5000) is ALSO consistent: mu .1344/.2948, alpha .0776/.3578, gap .1792/.2582, |z| <= 1.11. So q90 is excluded and q50-vs-dist is NOT identifiable from the control alone. Either way the numbers sit on a non-headline protocol. Cost to fix: one sentence.

0.362109375 = 0.9 x 0.40234375, and 0.40234375 is the mol_stability of EVERY unguided cell in results/sweep (fm_last, B200, batch 128, n=512, seed 20260921) — so the floor is itself a results/sweep number, contradicting the same section's rule that 'no BDG number may be compared to results/sweep'. Worse for seed 2: the repo's own seed-20260922 unguided cells give mol_stab 0.3691, floor 0.332227. Applying 0.362109 to seed-2 cells is 0.030 too strict, which is exactly the reported symptom ('gap fails it on seed 2, but so does its control'). BDG re-runs its own unguided control in every job, so the correct per-seed floor is free.

findings.claim: §5: 'No BDG number may be compared to results/sweep'
findings.evidence: Over-strict on generator grounds and unmeasured on device grounds. weights/fm_ema.pt records source_md5 a190ac8394902027d4a951f8d30e8c5c (= fm_last.pt), epoch 1500, identical training args, and weights/README.md states max|w_slim - w_full| = 0.0 — I verified the metadata directly. The repo has also measured device sensitivity: same config on RTX 5080 vs B200, largest cross-device |z| on in_band or stability = 1.77 and largest d(in_band) = 0.0024, with 0 flips for unguided. Right rule: aggregate comparisons are poolable with a stated caveat; paired molecule-level comparisons are not. CPU-vs-GPU and batch 512-vs-128 remain unmeasured, and BDG's own plug control is the free test (it agrees to <=0.67 sigma if the target is q50).
findings.refs: weights/README.md; fm_ema.pt metadata; docs/results/BTVG2_FULL_METRICS.md 'How much changing GPU moves a cell (measured)'

findings.claim: §6.1: 'a prior scan of 1,766 existing cells found the largest reproducible floor-clearing widening anywhere was 1.010x'
findings.evidence: I scanned all 1,478 fixed-target cells in results/sweep* (sd computed exactly as sqrt(RMSE^2 - bias^2), no distributional assumption; 774 have a matched unguided reference, 544 clear the 0.9x floor). Floor-clearing widening reaches 1.132x (alpha dflow q50 w4 tmin0.5, mol_stab 0.3906 vs floor 0.3621, 0 non-finite, 0 clipped steps), plus lgd_mc at 1.107/1.090/1.087/1.081; 6 cells > 1.05 and 2 > 1.10. DEFENCE FOR BDG: those widenings co-move the mean hard (dflow bias +11.4 delta vs unguided -0.78 delta; its in_band actually falls 0.0430 -> 0.0410), so they are not setpoint-addressed spread control. The claim should be restated as 'no existing arm widens at fixed centring' — which requires BDG's own bias numbers, which the handoff never reports. Only 72 configs exist in both seed trees, so 'not seed-reproducible' is untested rather than established.

findings.claim: §1/§6.1: 'monotone requested-to-achieved on 6/6 curves across two seeds ... Widening replicates on all three properties'
findings.evidence: Bootstrapped the se of an n=512 sd ratio from the real unguided f_B law (15,000 samples, 4,000 resamples): rel-se(sd) = 0.048/0.038/0.026 for mu/alpha/gap, so se(ratio of two independent cells) = 0.068/0.053/0.037 (normal theory would say 0.044 for all three). Widening z vs 1.0: mu +2.48 / +1.39, alpha +0.64 / +0.79, gap +2.59 / +3.16; pooling the two seeds gives +2.74 / +1.01 / +4.07. Alpha's widening is indistinguishable from none on both seeds. Tightening is solid: -3.86 / -5.99 / -5.75. Honest statement: the tightening direction is established, widening is established on gap, suggestive on mu, unsupported on alpha.

findings.claim: §9.1: the cells that beat plug while clearing the floor are eta=1 maxima over ~13 cells per property (alpha 0.0645 vs 0.0449; gap 0.1348 vs 0.1133)
findings.evidence: Quantified: at n=512 those are z = +1.38 (alpha) and +1.04 (gap), against this project's own pre-registered bar of z >= 3 with Holm adjustment within property (FULL_RUN_V2_PROTOCOL V7/V8). The intra-property maximum over ~13 cells makes the effective bar higher still. The handoff's self-warning is right and should be stated with these numbers rather than as a caveat; as written, a reader could take 0.0645 vs 0.0449 as a result.

findings.claim: Headline: 'tightening enough to matter breaks the chemistry floor, widening lowers coverage by definition' (§1)
findings.evidence: True at q50, false at q90 — and the handoff never states its target. Measured on 15,000 real unguided v2 samples, rescoring the same samples at both targets (unguided output is target-independent): at q90 bias/delta = -10.73/-20.52/-9.64, delta/sd = 0.108/0.057/0.167, best in_band over the whole scale grid is +0.0052/+0.0008/+0.0014 and the optimum is on the WIDENING side (s* = 1.20/1.40/1.10), while tightening to BDG's own 0.65 LOWERS in_band (mu .0355->.0232, alpha .0247->.0113, gap .0580->.0041). Debiasing buys +0.0477/+0.0236/+0.0506, i.e. 10-35x more. At q50 the picture inverts: bias/delta = +2.19/-0.76/-0.88 and tightening buys +0.233/+0.379/+0.428 while debiasing buys +0.004/-0.002/+0.005. So the geometric-impossibility sentence must carry its target, and at the project's headline target it is the tightening direction that is impossible.

findings.claim: Is 'spread control' a useful capability for THIS project's metrics (in_band at fixed q90), or only at q50?
findings.evidence: Only at q50, and the repo already held half the proof. results/btvg3_widening_sim.json (q90, real residuals from the same sidecars) reports widen_helps true for every arm with gain_widen +0.0019 to +0.0069 against gain_debias +0.0253 to +0.0325 — the same ordering my independent counterfactual finds. Consequence for the paper: BDG's capability is real but is pointed at a lever worth <=0.005 in_band at the headline target, and the defensible framing is 'we built a controller for the quantity that governs coverage at a median target, then measured that at the upper-decile target the residual is bias-dominated, so the lever is worth ~1/10 of debiasing'. That sentence is worth §4.3 + §4.7 + Discussion credit and costs no new runs.

findings.claim: Could BDG's capability be recast as useful for a distribution-matching objective (the 'dist' protocol)?
findings.evidence: Measured on the v1 dist n=5000 sidecars: scaling the batch spread of f_B about its mean buys at most +0.013 in_band on unguided (s* 0.20-0.80, 3 seeds) and +0.0004 / +0.0000 / +0.0000 at plug w=4 (s* = 1.00 on gap and mu). Reason: under per-molecule targets the coverage-limiting quantity is corr(F,y), which rises 0.131-0.586 (unguided) to 0.681-0.804 (plug w=4) — a per-molecule tracking property no batch-variance setpoint can address; residual sd is 4.8-15.7 delta while bias is only 0.04-2.2 delta. There is also no distribution-matching metric to reward it: evaluate_samples has no W1/KS/coverage-of-target-law term, and the only spread-sensitive metrics (diversity_mean_pairwise, diversity_logdet, uniqueness) already favour the guided arms (alpha: lgd_mc 1.2361 vs unguided 1.2204; uniqueness 1.000, lowest single cell 0.9934), so 'restore collapsed diversity' is not a live need either.
findings.refs: scratchpad/bdg/dist_lever.py and dist_lever.json; proj1/src/evaluation.py; v2 metric block computed from results/full/v2/n5000

findings.claim: §3: 'The loop self-limits ... A fixed schedule cannot do that' (listed in §7 as verified: 'open-loop control does not reproduce it')
findings.evidence: Two independent problems. (1) Internal contradiction: §9.2 reports plug at a constant negative w widening 1.153x at mol_stab 0.397, against BDG's 1.034 at 0.373 on alpha — a fixed weight reaches MORE of the capability at BETTER chemistry. What fails to reproduce is one particular schedule (the time-average of w_eff), not the family. (2) The operating points are computable and show why: with s = f_A.y_std (1.5394 / 8.2004 / 0.047462) and the measured unguided batch sd (1.5517 / 8.4149 / 0.04537), V_b/s^2 = 1.016 / 1.053 / 0.914, so at tau_mult 1.5, eta 4, e = -0.548 / -0.532 / -0.594 and w_eff = 1 + eta*e = -1.19 / -1.13 / -1.38 — the e4t1.5 'widening' cells run at a NEGATIVE effective guidance weight, i.e. they ARE §9.2's negative-w plug up to the feedback. At tau_mult 0.5 the same arithmetic gives w_eff = +13.2 / +13.8 / +11.6 and y_eff = 0.92*F_bar + 0.08*y: the tightening cells are plug at ~13x weight aimed 92% at the batch's own mean, which explains the chemistry-floor failure and the flat in_band without any variance narrative. The paper must not claim 'no fixed schedule reproduces it' from the time-average control alone; the matched-spread plug control (plan item B2) is the one that settles it.
findings.refs: handoff §3, §7, §9.2; weights/f_A_*.pt (y_std); unguided sd from results/full/v2/n5000 sidecars

findings.claim: §10: 'five ablations exist' for §4.4
findings.evidence: The template requires, for a single atomic change, 'at least two informative controls, such as ... matched hyperparameter controls', and 'A strong ablation does more than show that the final system is best; it demonstrates which proposed mechanism is responsible for the improvement.' Of the five listed, eta=0 == plug is a correctness gate (it MUST be bit-identical) and the one-sided cell at t1.5 does nothing by construction (clamped, asked to widen) — a grader can reasonably count both as gates. The genuinely informative three are the tau ladder, V_b vs V_F, and the w_eff control, which still clears the bar, but the w_eff control is the weak variant. Also note the rubric's wording assumes an improvement to attribute; with a null, §4.4's .675 cannot be earned in full however good the controls are.

findings.claim: §2: 'Cost: zero extra NFE. Cost dict is byte-identical to plug.'

objections.title: 'The loop does not reduce to any fixed weight schedule' (§3, §7, §8(d)) rests on a confounded control and fails the clean one
objections.argument: §3 concedes BDG is plug at a rescaled weight aiming at a shifted target, then rests its novelty on the feedback: freezing w_eff at its time-average and running plug fails to reproduce BDG (mu 2.53x vs 1.17x). That control changes three things at once: it removes time variation, removes the feedback, and drops the y_eff shift, because the plug arm aims at y. It also freezes to a value the trajectory barely visits (w_eff spans [-2.64, +10.35] and changes sign up to 34 times in 50 steps). The clean control is to replay the recorded schedule open-loop on fresh noise. That lands within 0.3-6.6% of the closed loop on 8/8 configs, against 8.4-30.5% for plug, so it closes 73-96% of the gap and sits inside the ~4.4% noise floor. Deterministic replay is exact to 4e-17. A fitted loop gain predicts the frozen control within ~7%, not a 6x log-widening gap. §9.2's constant negative-w plug (1.153x at mol_stab 0.397) contradicts §7. What survives is approximate cross-batch transfer (5-17% miss in the toy), which leaves BDG one sentence from assignment §3.5's exclusion of ordinary hyperparameter tuning.

objections.title: The unstated target is q50; the §1 premise and the §1/§4.7 'impossibility' result reverse at the project's q90 headline
objections.argument: The plug w=4 control matches results/sweep q50 (chi2 1.4, p 0.96) and is excluded at q90 (chi2 24.7, p ~4e-4). A third run agrees. At q90, on 15,000 real v2 unguided samples, debiasing buys +0.047/+0.025/+0.048 in_band and the best spread change buys at most +0.004/+0.001/+0.001. The spread optimum is on the widening side (s* 1.20/1.40/1.10, which matches the Gaussian |b|/sigma), and tightening to 0.65 lowers in_band. The GPU port shows the same sign flip (q50 3/3 down, q90 2/3 up, each within ~1 se). §1's supporting statistic, delta/sigma 0.056-0.169, does not depend on the target; the regime is set by |bias|/sigma (0.05-0.23 at q50 against 1.19-1.60 at q90). results/btvg3_widening_sim.json already records widen_helps = true on all 15 q90 cells. The 'tightening breaks chemistry' half is an observation confounded with effective strength (see the strength-ladder objection), and the §6.2 row it rests on depends on a borrowed floor. Putting the impossibility result forward as a headline, as proposed, would place a false general statement in §4.7.

objections.title: Widening is negative-weight plug and the tau ladder is a strength ladder, so spread is not decoupled from centring and §6.3's core result has no plug control
objections.argument: The deviation dynamics are d <- d(1-kappa*w_eff), so spread grows only when w_eff < 0. Widening cells therefore run plug at a negative weight: run-means -0.13 to -0.84, single steps down to -2.64. Tightening cells run at +2.1 to +3.7 on average, up to +10.35 per step (about +13 at the first step), aimed 92% at the batch mean, which explains the §6.2 chemistry failures. Chemistry tracks |w_eff| (corr -0.40) more than tau (+0.31). BDG is still one knob: bias/delta moves 0.35-1.83 delta along the ladder, MAE/delta degrades in 5/6 blocks, and the mean drag is exactly w_eff times plug's drag. §6.3 compares BDG's 31-43% spread range with btvg_var's but has no plug row, and plain plug sweeps 19.5-38.9% on the same grid. btvg_var also ran at batch 128 against BDG's 512, so the two arms saw different molecules. The one supported mechanism (V_b survives while V_F vanishes) is already established in VARIANCE_DECOMPOSITION.md, along with an unguided re-widening caveat the handoff omits.

objections.title: The stability and fixed-point claims are wrong: V* = tau^2(1-1/eta), not tau^2, and eta=1 cannot widen
objections.argument: 'V_b does not vanish, so the fixed point is stable' is a non-sequitur. Stability needs a gain bound (kappa < 1/(eta-1), plus a transient bound kappa < 2/w_eff(u0), with divergence at 0.154), needs eta > 1, and needs bounded estimator noise; the handoff states none of these. The interior equilibrium is V* = tau^2(1-1/eta), verified to ~1e-15, so at eta=4 the requested sd is undershot by 13.4%. That explains §9.6's 'unexplained' alpha 0.84-0.87 as sqrt(0.75). The runs never reach V* in 50 steps (V_b/tau^2 1.27-1.68 against 0.75), so tau acts as an initial gain rather than a setpoint. At eta=1, w_eff >= 0 and V* = 0 (asked to widen 4x, V falls from 1.0 to 0.062). The bound that actually licenses dropping the clamp is algebraic: V_b >= 0 gives e >= -1, so w_eff >= 1-eta. The handoff omits it.

objections.title: 'No existing arm widens reproducibly' is false (rch 1.42-1.45x, dflow 1.13x), the 1.010x yardstick is noise, and BDG's alpha widening is inside noise
objections.argument: rch on alpha at q50, w=0.05 widens 1.4231x and 1.4548x on both seeds, clears the floor, has 0 non-finite samples, and sits on a monotone ladder. 32 keys widen and clear on every seed, and dflow reaches 1.132x. The 1,766-cell count only works with 216 EDMsecond cells from another base model. At n=512, P(ratio > 1.010 | null) is 0.39-0.44. BDG's alpha widening (1.034/1.042) is 0.6/0.8 se, and mu seed 2 is 1.4 se, so widening is established only on gap. Tightening is solid (z -3.9 to -6.0). The distinctive claim, widening at fixed centring, is unevidenced because no bias/delta is reported and bias moves by up to 1.83 delta.

objections.title: The chemistry floor is borrowed from the forbidden results/sweep source, is wrong for seed 2, and decides §6.2's load-bearing row
objections.argument: §5 forbids comparing BDG with results/sweep, yet the floor 0.362109375 is 0.9 x the results/sweep unguided value 0.40234375. The noise is drawn per batch (sampling.py:603), so BDG's 512 molecules are an independent sample (se 0.0216). The pooled truth is 0.3968, and seed 2's own unguided value is 0.3691 (floor 0.3322). The gap e4t0.5 row, which the handoff reports as FAILS, would pass against a fresh control with probability 0.31. Each job re-runs unguided, so the per-seed floor was available. objection.evidence: [gpu#12] 8/8, one seed pair, 2 props x 2 tau; [novelty#3] 4.2e-17/5.6e-17, transfer miss 17%/5%; [math#18]; [doable#16]; [doable#3]; BDG_HANDOFF.md §3 lines 104-107, §7 line 243, §8 lines 259-260, §9.3-9.4 lines 279-283

defence.argument:
CONCEDED. (1) The sentence "does not reduce to any fixed weight schedule" (§3, §7, §8(d)) is false as written. On a deterministic sampler, any closed-loop run can be replayed as an open-loop schedule on its own noise and reproduced exactly. The GPU pipeline is deterministic here: two separate seed-A runs agree on w_eff to 2e-7. (2) The handoff's control is confounded. Freezing w_eff at its time-average changes three things at once, so it separates constant from time-varying, not open-loop from closed-loop. It should be withdrawn as evidence. (3) Within one configuration, the spread LEVEL is carried by the schedule. A replayed e-schedule lands within 0.3-6.6% of the closed loop's achieved sd, while plug w=1 lands 8.4-30.5% away. (4) §9.2 does not logically contradict §7, but it removes the practical point. A constant negative w widens further (1.153x on alpha) with better chemistry, so widening itself does not need the loop.

REBUTTED. Three legs of the objection overreach.
(a) "Inside the ~4.4% noise floor" is a category error. Replay and closed both run on seed B's noise, and the pipeline is deterministic, so the paired null is about 1e-7, not 4.4%. Every bit of |replay-closed| is the effect of the batch-specific part of the schedule. That the effect is noise-sized is exactly what a regulator does: it cancels disturbances of noise size. The right test compares seed-to-seed variation under each policy using the same schedule source:
- Closed loop: |C(B)-C(A)|.
- Open loop: |R(B)-C(A)|, where C(A) is e_A applied to noise A.
The result splits by branch:
- Tightening (w_eff>0, contractive): open loop 1.1%, closed loop 2.6%. The schedule is enough, and I concede this branch.
- Widening (w_eff<0, expansive): closed loop 2.0%, open loop 5.2%, iid expectation 6.0%. Under an iid null the closed loop's variation has P=0.016 and the open loop's P=0.55. |R-C| exceeds |C-A| on 4/4 widening configs and 0/4 tightening configs.
- Gap shows it most clearly: the closed loop lands seed B within 0.44% and 0.03% of seed A, while the replayed schedule misses by 2.9% and 6.7%. It does this with a schedule correction of only 0.08 rms in w_eff.
This branch split is predicted, not post-hoc. Widening requires w_eff<0, where deviations grow under any fixed schedule (math#6). A toy set to the measured gains gives an open/closed ratio of 2.8-6.6x when widening against 1.5-2.2x when tightening. Its paired misses (0.054-0.072 vs 0.026-0.045) bracket the GPU values (0.051 vs 0.018).
(b) The "fitted gain predicts the frozen control within ~7%" argument rests on kappa=0.001-0.003. The logged per-step trajectories contradict that. An OLS fit of dlogV on w_eff over the first 20 guided steps gives k=0.32-0.34 for mu and 0.10-0.12 for gap (R^2 0.89-0.97), 54-170x the fitted value. Those gains also explain the observed shapes under math#7's own stability bands:
- mu sits at 1/(eta-1)=0.333, which gives damped period-2 ringing (14-34 sign changes observed).
- gap sits below 1/6, which gives a monotone approach (0-1 sign changes observed).
At a gain of 0.30, the math lens's own g_openloop.py with a clip gives frozen 1.67x against BDG 1.30x, the same direction as the handoff's 2.53x-vs-1.17x result. The ~7% prediction therefore does not hold, though the confound in (2) still does.
(c) "One sentence from §3.5's exclusion" goes too far. The rubric excludes retuning a scalar and running larger sweeps. It lists a new guidance mechanism or a sampler-level change as valid, and it asks for "matched hyperparameter controls" as §4.4 ablations, which is where the replay belongs. The recorded schedules are specific to each configuration: at the same tau, the rms difference across properties is 1.68/0.82, against 0.51/0.37 across seeds. So the transferable object is tau_mult, and each schedule is an output of the loop, not a hyperparameter. The real exposure is novelty against the feedback-guidance literature, not the rubric.

LIMITS. This rests on one seed pair and 4 configs per branch. mu does not show regulation (1 of 2), which fits a loop at its stability margin. My portability check was inconclusive: across configs, the achieved-ratio sd is 0.031-0.055 for BDG against 0.062-0.069 for plug, but all of it sits inside a conservative noise band. The replay also keeps F_bar live, so it speaks to spread and not to bias. The narrower claim is defensible only once the proposed experiment backs it.

defence.proposed_experiment:
Regulation test on the local RTX 5080 using the existing worktree port (bdg_e_override), fm_ema.pt, n=256 in one batch, eta=4.
- Configs: {mu, alpha, gap} x q50 x tau_mult {0.5, 1.5}, i.e. 6 configs.
- Per config:
  1. Closed loop on seeds s1-s6 (6 cells).
  2. Replay s1's recorded e-schedule on s2-s6 (5 cells).
  3. Matched-constant control: plug at the constant w that reproduces closed-s1's achieved sd, found by a 3-4 point bisection on s1 and then run on s2-s6 (about 9 cells).
- Add mu at eta=2 as a gain check (11 cells).
- Pre-registered predictions:
  - Widening: seed-to-seed sd of achieved sd(f_A) is at least 2x larger under replay and under the constant than under the closed loop, on gap and alpha.
  - Tightening: the ratio is at most 1.5.
  - mu at eta=4 may fail; mu at eta=2 should pass.
- Also report bias/delta and mol_stab per cell.
- Cost: about 131 cells x 21 s, roughly 46 min of GPU on the 5080 (about 1.5 h with q90 added). Add 5 cells per config for a pure plug-schedule replay (w_eff(t), y_eff(t) from s1, live F_bar cut) if any bias or in_band claim is made.
- Decision rule: if the widening ratio is below 1.5, drop §8(d) entirely and describe BDG only as a setpoint-driven schedule generator.
defence.proposed_revision:
§3, replace lines 104-107 ("What does NOT reduce: the feedback ... Cells: results/bdg/*__plug__*weff*.json.") with:

"**What the feedback adds.** Over a run BDG is plug under a time-varying schedule (w_eff(t), y_eff(t)). On a deterministic sampler, replaying the realised schedule on the same noise reproduces the run exactly, so BDG is not irreducible to a schedule. Replayed open-loop on fresh noise (n=256, one seed pair, mu/gap x q50/q90 x tau_mult 0.5/1.5), a recorded schedule lands within 0.3-6.6% of the closed loop's achieved spread (plug w=1: 8.4-30.5%). Widening runs at w_eff<0: there the loop's seed-to-seed change in achieved sd is 2.0% (gap: 0.44%, 0.03%) against 5.2% for its own schedule replayed (gap: 2.9%, 6.7%). Tightening is contractive, and the replay is as reproducible as the loop (1.1% vs 2.6%). mu at eta=4 is the exception: its measured per-step gain (~0.33) sits at the loop's oscillation bound 1/(eta-1). This is provisional, from one seed pair. The earlier frozen-time-average control changed three things at once and is withdrawn. Recorded schedules differ 2-3x more across properties than across seeds, so tau_mult is the portable knob, not a schedule."

§7, reduction row: "w_eff factorisation verified to 1e-14. A recorded schedule replayed open-loop on fresh noise reproduces the achieved spread to 0.3-6.6% (8 configs, 1 seed pair). The loop's residual role is seed-to-seed regulation in the widening branch (provisional)."

§8, replace "(d) the demonstration that the resulting loop does not reduce to any fixed weight schedule" with: "the measurement that the feedback matters only in the widening branch. There, negative effective weight makes open-loop guidance expansive, and the loop holds the achieved spread across seeds where its own replayed schedule does not (provisional)."

§9.2, append: "With §3 this means widening itself is not unique to the loop. What the loop claims is reproducibility of a requested spread without a per-configuration search, which the matched-constant control must test."

ruling.rationale:
I checked the handoff's text and re-derived the defence's numbers from d1_paired_replay.json and d2_loop_gain.json.

The core of the objection stands, and the defence concedes it. §3 lines 104-107, the §7 reduction row ("open-loop control does not reproduce it") and §8(d) all rest on one control. That control froze w_eff at its time-average, but the recorded trajectory spans [-2.64, +10.35] with up to 34 sign changes. The control also dropped the y_eff shift and removed the feedback, so it changed three things at once. A deterministic sampler can always replay a closed-loop run exactly on its own noise (toy: 4e-17). On fresh noise, the replayed e-schedule lands within 0.3-6.6% of the closed loop's achieved sd, against 8.4-30.5% for plug (I confirmed rc and pc in the json). So the spread level is carried by the schedule, and "does not reduce to any fixed weight schedule" is false.

Three legs of the attack overreach. The defence rebuts each correctly.
(a) The "inside the ~4.4% noise floor" comparison is a category error. Replay and closed loop share seed-B noise, and the pipeline is deterministic (reruns match to about 1e-8). So |R-C| is a real, if small, effect of the batch-specific part of the schedule, not sampling noise.
(b) The claim that the loop moves w_eff only ~7% is contradicted by the attack's own gpu#12 trajectory. d2 also shows that the h_calibrate gain underpredicts the per-step max dlogV by 20-150x (model_max 0.004-0.04 vs observed 0.16-1.25).
(c) Calling BDG "one sentence from the §3.5 exclusion" is rhetoric. The rubric counts a new guidance mechanism as an innovation. The real exposure is prior art (Feedback Guidance 2506.06085, MGD), not the rubric.

The defence's positive claim, that the loop regulates spread only in the widening branch, is not established:
- It rests on one seed pair and 4 configs per branch, and mu splits 1-1. On mu q50 t1.5, open loop gives 0.4% and closed loop 3.3%.
- The widening P=0.016 comes mostly from the two gap cells (ca 0.0044 and 0.0003). The mean open-loop figure of 5.2% is driven by mu q90 (0.106).
- The d3 toy was tuned to gains measured after the data were seen.
- The d2 gains are selective and confounded. k=0.32-0.34 holds only at tau 1.0/1.5, while the tau 0.5 fits give 0.06-0.12 at R^2 0.40-0.62. dlogV regressed on w_eff also picks up the flow's own non-monotone variance drift, since w_eff is a function of V.
- The same chi2 applied to the open loop in the tightening branch gives about 0.34 on 4 dof, P about 0.013. That is as "sub-iid" as the closed loop in the widening branch, so reproducibility below the iid level does not by itself point to feedback.
- The proposed revision's wording is not accurate. Tightening replay (1.1%) is about 2.4x more reproducible than the loop (2.6%), not "as reproducible".
- All of this runs on the reviewer's local re-port with fm_ema.pt at n=256, not on Bobo's code.

So the revision's removals and its schedule-transfer text are sound. Promoting "regulation in the widening branch" to a §8 "what is ours" item is premature.

objection.title: The unstated target is q50; the §1 premise and the §1/§4.7 'impossibility' result reverse at the project's q90 headline
objection.argument: The plug w=4 control matches results/sweep q50 (chi2 1.4, p 0.96) and is excluded at q90 (chi2 24.7, p ~4e-4). A third run agrees. At q90, on 15,000 real v2 unguided samples, debiasing buys +0.047/+0.025/+0.048 in_band and the best spread change buys at most +0.004/+0.001/+0.001. The spread optimum is on the widening side (s* 1.20/1.40/1.10, which matches the Gaussian |b|/sigma), and tightening to 0.65 lowers in_band. The GPU port shows the same sign flip (q50 3/3 down, q90 2/3 up, each within ~1 se). §1's supporting statistic, delta/sigma 0.056-0.169, does not depend on the target; the regime is set by |bias|/sigma (0.05-0.23 at q50 against 1.19-1.60 at q90). results/btvg3_widening_sim.json already records widen_helps = true on all 15 q90 cells. The 'tightening breaks chemistry' half is an observation confounded with effective strength (see the strength-ladder objection), and the §6.2 row it rests on depends on a borrowed floor. Putting the impossibility result forward as a headline, as proposed, would place a false general statement in §4.7.

defence.argument:
I concede every factual part of the objection. I rebut only the word "fatal": the objection damages the framing, not the method, and the negative result can still headline §4.7 if it is restated as a two-regime result that depends on the target.

CONCEDED
(1) BDG ran at q50. There are two independent statistical triangulations, and the handoff's own text adds a third line: §3 says "Both w_eff and y_eff are single numbers shared by the batch". That can only be true if y is a scalar target, so dist (per-molecule y_i) is ruled out. This closes the q50-vs-dist ambiguity that doable#7 left open.
(2) §1's premise is not a general fact. δ/σ does not depend on the target, so it cannot decide which lever governs. |b|/σ decides it.
(3) "Widening lowers coverage by definition" is false at q90. There the optimum is on the widening side (s* ≈ |b|/σ), and tightening to 0.65 lowers in_band.
(4) "We can prove" is wrong for the tightening half. It is an observation, and it is weaker than §1 says even at q50. In this repo's own seed-1 sweep, floor-clearing cells on mu and alpha tighten to sd/unguided 0.63-0.67 (tfg_mc w=4, btvg w=4). Plug w=4 on alpha misses the floor by 0.0008 on seed 1 and passes on seed 2. Only gap holds cleanly: 0 of 11 (seed 1) and 0 of 1 (seed 2) cells with sd/unguided ≤ 0.80 clear the floor.

REBUTTED
(a) The objection is not fatal to the method's validity. It targets the §1 motivation and a sentence proposed for §4.7. The mechanism does not depend on the target: the GPU port found the requested-to-achieved spread monotone on all three q90 curves (0.73-1.22) as well as the three q50 curves.
(b) Within the plug family, the "strength confound" on the tightening half is not a confound. §3 proves BDG is in that family. The deviation dynamics are d_i <- d_i(1 - κ w_eff), so contracting the spread and applying effective strength are the same quantity. The claim is wrong only when it is extended to "any spread knob".
(c) Most importantly, the reversal at q90 does not rescue spread control. It makes the negative result stronger, and at q90 that result no longer needs a chemistry argument. On 15,000 real unguided v2 samples, the best spread setting at q90 in either direction buys:
- continuous: +0.0049 / +0.0023 / +0.0022
- decoded: +0.0056 / +0.0014 / +0.0019
Inside the range BDG can actually reach (0.65-1.22), decoded alpha gains only +0.0001. Treated as an unpaired sampler comparison, the best gain has z = 0.43 / 0.24 / 0.15 at BDG's n=512. It is still only 2.3 / 1.3 / 0.8 (decoded 2.6 / 0.8 / 0.7) at 15,000 samples per arm, the project's whole v2 budget, which is below the project's own z≥3 bar. So "no spread setting BDG can reach yields an in_band gain this project could certify" is TRUE at both targets, for different reasons:
- q50: the lever is large, but pulling it costs strength, and that strength costs the chemistry floor (cleanly on gap).
- q90: the lever is too small to detect, and it points toward widening.
(d) The boundary is measurable, and it is useful to the paper. Rescoring at QM9 quantiles q50 to q95, the debias gain overtakes the spread gain at about q0.72-0.78 (|b|/σ ≈ 0.6-0.9) for all three properties. s* crosses 1 at |b|/σ ≈ 1.0-1.2 (about q0.85-0.90). This also explains why the project's q90 headline is limited by centring (v2 bias/δ −9 to −21), which is §4.3 material.

So I would keep the negative result as the §4.7 headline in the revised, target-conditioned form below, and not in the §1/§10 form, which the objection correctly shows is false as a general statement.

ruling.rationale:
I re-derived both halves of the objection myself, using scratchpad/bdg/judge_q90/judge_check.py. The script is independent of both sides' code.

(1) Target. BDG's plug w=4 control fits results/sweep plug w=4 t_min 0.5 at q50 with chi2(6)=1.44 and is excluded at q90 with chi2(6)=24.73. This reproduces data#1 exactly. The v1 dist run is also consistent (doable#7: |z|<=1.11; data#1: chi2 3.4). So the evidence rules out q90, but it does not fully separate q50 from dist. The defence's pointer to §3 line 94 ("w_eff and y_eff are single numbers shared by the batch") supports q50 but does not prove it. Either way, the §1 premise is not the project's headline protocol: doable#15 shows the spread lever is worth <=0.013 under dist as well.

(2) Lever. On the 15,000 pooled v2 unguided sidecars, rescored at each target, I reproduced every number both sides cite:
- q90, |b|/sd: 1.199 / 1.187 / 1.599.
- q90, debias gain: +0.047 / +0.025 / +0.047 (decoded +0.048 / +0.024 / +0.051).
- q90, best spread gain: +0.0049 / +0.0023 / +0.0022, at s* = 1.18 / 1.37 / 1.04, which is on the widening side.
- q90, tightening to s=0.65 lowers in_band: .0347 -> .0225, .0241 -> .0109, .0594 -> .0041.
- delta/sd is 0.110 / 0.057 / 0.167 at both targets.

So as written, §1's premise, its supporting statistic, the sentence "widening lowers coverage by definition", and the "we can prove" impossibility (§1 lines 20-22; §6.2 line 219; §10 lines 299-300) are all false at the project's headline target. Every factual part of the objection holds, and the defence concedes all of it.

Where the defence is right:
- The objection is not fatal to the method. The requested-to-achieved spread mapping is independent of the target (gpu#7: monotone on 6/6 curves, including 3 at q90).
- A negative result conditioned on the target survives.
- At q90 the whole spread lever is below detection: unpaired z <= 2.6 even at n=15,000 per arm.
- The tightening half is, within the plug family, the same thing as effective strength (math#6 and gpu#13: d_i <- d_i(1 - kappa*w_eff)). That makes it a strength/chemistry trade-off, not a separate spread failure.

Where the defence's own replacement text overreaches:
(a) The claim that spread control "cannot deliver a certifiable in_band gain at EITHER target" is not established at q50. Inside BDG's reachable range (s=0.65) the pure-spread lever at q50 is large and resolvable: +0.049 / +0.026 / +0.055, unpaired z of 8-14 at n=512. So the q50 negative rests entirely on the chemistry floor. The defence itself concedes that holds cleanly only on gap. Floor-clearing cells tighten to 0.63-0.67 on mu and alpha (tfg_mc w=4 on mu, btvg w=4 on alpha). The decisive BDG gap row (e4t0.5) fails only against a borrowed floor, with a 0.31 chance that BDG's own unguided control would flip it (data#8). At q50 the honest statement is "BDG did not, at n=512", not "cannot".
(b) The revision quotes the q50 tightening gain at s=0.3 (+0.11 to +0.23). BDG cannot reach that; its tightest cell is sd/unguided 0.65. The quantile crossover it cites (about q0.72-0.78) also uses that idealised lever. Within BDG's reach the crossover comes earlier.
(c) The counterfactual holds the centre fixed. BDG does not: gpu#11 shows bias moving by 0.35-1.83 delta along the tau ladder. The paper must say the rescoring is an idealised pure-spread bound, not a BDG prediction.

In short: the objection stands against the claim, the defence stands against the word "fatal", and the proposed revision is accepted with the corrections listed below.

objection.title: Widening is negative-weight plug and the tau ladder is a strength ladder, so spread is not decoupled from centring and §6.3's core result has no plug control
objection.argument: The deviation dynamics are d <- d(1-kappa*w_eff), so spread grows only when w_eff < 0. Widening cells therefore run plug at a negative weight: run-means -0.13 to -0.84, single steps down to -2.64. Tightening cells run at +2.1 to +3.7 on average, up to +10.35 per step (about +13 at the first step), aimed 92% at the batch mean, which explains the §6.2 chemistry failures. Chemistry tracks |w_eff| (corr -0.40) more than tau (+0.31). BDG is still one knob: bias/delta moves 0.35-1.83 delta along the ladder, MAE/delta degrades in 5/6 blocks, and the mean drag is exactly w_eff times plug's drag. §6.3 compares BDG's 31-43% spread range with btvg_var's but has no plug row, and plain plug sweeps 19.5-38.9% on the same grid. btvg_var also ran at batch 128 against BDG's 512, so the two arms saw different molecules. The one supported mechanism (V_b survives while V_F vanishes) is already established in VARIANCE_DECOMPOSITION.md, along with an unguided re-widening caveat the handoff omits.

defence.argument:
REBUT the core inference; CONCEDE the §6.3 control, the batch mismatch and the citation.

1. The objection gets from "plug at w_eff aiming at y_eff" (§3) to "negative-weight plug" by dropping y_eff. Keep it and the numerator splits exactly:
   num_i = (y - F_bar) - w_eff (F_i - F_bar)   [BDG]
   num_i = w (y - F_bar) - w (F_i - F_bar)     [plug at w]
Identity: w_eff (y_eff - F_bar) = y - F_bar. So BDG always pulls the batch mean toward y at unit gain, and only the deviation gain is w_eff. Plug ties the two gains together at w, so the plug arm at w<0 pushes the mean AWAY from y. BDG widening is negative gain on the deviation mode only, not negative-weight plug. math#12's own formula says the same thing (mean move = (y-F_bar)mean(a)/s^2 - w_eff mean(d a)/s^2): w_eff multiplies only the second-order covariance drag, never the centring term. The objection quotes only the drag half. This does not reopen "new direction", which §3 already concedes. It says BDG splits plug's one strength into two gains: centring fixed at 1, dispersion servoed. That split is what "decoupled" means.

2. The prediction holds on the red team's own cells (n=256, seed 20260925, paired noise; no new sampling). At q90 plug's centring step is large, so a centring gain tied to w_eff would move the bias 9.4 / 5.2 / 29.4 delta (gap/mu/alpha) over the ladder's w_eff span. Observed: 0.61 / 1.21 / 1.88. The ladder slope d(bias)/d(w_eff) is +0.04 / -0.24 / -0.02 of plug's slope.
- gap q90 t1.5 has w_eff < 0 at all 50 guided steps ([-2.64, -0.35]). It still keeps 86% of plug w=1's debias: bias -7.36 against -9.97 unguided and -6.95 for plug w=1.
- Negative-weight plug at the same run-mean weight would sit at -12.36. The t1.5 cells beat that prediction by +5.0 / +3.1 / +8.7 delta (paired z 14.8 / 5.1 / 13.6; at least about 5 after also counting the error in the prediction).
- The extrapolation understates the gap, because plug's bias response is concave: the small-w slope in results/sweep is 1.3-2x the 0->1 secant.
- The tightening end also sits at plug w=1's centring, not at plug-at-w_eff's. e4t0.5 bias is -7.09 / -8.30 / -14.00, against -6.95 / -8.16 / -12.12 for plug w=1 and about -6.1 / -6.7 / -9.4 for plug interpolated at w_eff.
So the tau ladder is a ladder in dispersion gain at fixed centring gain, not a strength ladder.

3. "Explains the chemistry failures": partial. Within blocks, chemistry does track |w_eff| (corr -0.55 vs +0.44 for tau, and |w_eff| and tau are collinear at -0.76), so the dispersion push is not free. But at matched spread at q90 (sd/ug 0.742/0.739/0.730 vs plug w=4's 0.719/0.719/0.751), BDG e4t0.5 has mol_stab +0.082 / +0.141 / +0.086 above plug w=4 (paired z 2.7 / 4.7 / 2.4). Tightening costs chemistry, but less than getting the same tightening from plug, which must also push the mean 4x harder. At q50 this is not established (+0.055 / +0.070 / +0.008, z 1.6 / 2.2 / 0.2; spreads not matched).

4. The rise in MAE/delta along the ladder is spread, not centring. Recentring each cell to plug w=1's bias leaves MAE almost unchanged (alpha q90 t1.5: 18.80 -> 17.88; mu q90 t1.5: 11.36 -> 11.91). So it is not evidence of coupling.

CONCESSIONS.
(a) §6.3 has no plug row, and spread range cannot tell a dispersion controller from a strength sweep. results/sweep plug moves sd/ug by 21.7-36.1% (one-sided: it never widens). The statistic that does separate them is sd range per delta of bias swing: plug 2.8-16.2% (75% on gap q50, where the target sits at the mean), btvg_var 0.6-11.6%, BDG 28-92%. Caveat: the BDG ladder numbers come from the port (5080, n=256), not the handoff's CPU cells.
(b) The claim "same checkpoint, seed, device and window, so valid" is false on batch (128 vs 512). But sd-ratio noise at n=512 is 0.04-0.07, and a same-batch results/sweep run confirms btvg_var's range is narrow (2.7-15.5%). So the batch mismatch does not produce the V_b-vs-V_F contrast.
(c) VARIANCE_DECOMPOSITION.md already measured V_b vs V_F and must be cited. It is a diagnostic, not a controller, so it is a premise, not prior art. Its unguided re-widening caveat does not touch sd/unguided ratios, which are netted against an unguided control; it does affect any within-trajectory attribution.
(d) At the handoff's own target (q50) the batch sits 1-3 delta off target and plug's mean step is small (-0.26 on gap; +1.47 on alpha, and that one is away from target). So BDG widening and negative-w plug nearly coincide there, which is why §9.2's comparator competes on alpha. The split only shows off-target, and today that evidence is one seed of the red-team port.
(e) Residual mean leakage of 0.4-1.9 delta is real, not zero.

ruling.rationale:
The core inference is rebutted. The objection's minor points stand and the defence concedes them.

1. The algebra favours the defence. (y−F_i) − ηe(F_i−F̄) = (y−F̄) − (1+ηe)(F_i−F̄) is exact, and mode_split.txt Part A gives 1e-14. The batch-mean coefficient of the BDG numerator is the nominal w (here 1) at every η and τ. Only the deviation mode sees w_eff. Plug at weight w puts w on both. So "widening = negative-weight plug" is false as stated. It holds for the deviation mode only. The attack's "mean drag is exactly w_eff × plug's drag" quotes only the covariance-drag term from math#12, whose own formula keeps (y−F̄)·mean(a)/s² separate. gpu#11's reading that the bias swing "can only arrive through w_eff multiplying the centring term" is therefore wrong. The swing comes through cov(|J^T g|², F−F̄).

2. I checked this on the port's paired cells (scratchpad/bdg/cells, n=256, seed 20260925), without the defence's linear extrapolation. At q90 the widening cells e4t1.5 move the batch mean TOWARD the target relative to unguided: +2.61 / +2.88 / +5.43 δ (gap/mu/alpha), paired z 7.7 / 4.7 / 8.5. Plug w=1 moves it +3.02 / +1.80 / +7.04. Gap t1.5 has w_eff<0 at every step. A negative-weight plug would push the mean away from y to first order, so the qualitative rebuttal does not depend on the extrapolated −12.4 / −10.2 / −22.4 figures, which are crude, as the alpha t0.5 "plugLck +7.0" value shows. Ladder bias swing is 0.36–1.88 δ against plug's own 2.2–9.5 δ. The τ ladder is a dispersion-gain ladder at fixed centring gain, not a pure strength ladder.

3. What stands against the handoff:
- §6.3 has no plug row. Plug alone moves sd/ug 21.7–36.1% on the same grid (controls.txt §3), so spread range cannot discriminate a dispersion controller from a strength sweep.
- The "same checkpoint, seed, device and window so valid" sentence omits batch 128 vs 512, which the handoff itself admits in §5.
- VARIANCE_DECOMPOSITION.md is uncited.
- Chemistry tracks |w_eff| (within-block −0.55; raw −0.37 to −0.40). The dispersion push is itself a strength with a chemistry price, so "tightening costs chemistry" is really "|w_eff| costs chemistry".
- The leakage of 0.4–1.9 δ is not zero. On gap/mu q50 it is comparable to plug's own centring moves, so "decoupled" is too strong.
- Most important: the handoff ran at q50. There my check shows the split is barely visible: gap q50 mean shift +0.17 δ (z 0.6), mu q50 −0.86 δ (z −1.6). So on the handoff's own data, BDG widening and negative-w plug nearly coincide, and §9.2's competitor is live.

4. The defence's matched-spread chemistry point (e4t0.5 vs plug w4: +0.08 / +0.14 / +0.09, z 2.7 / 4.7 / 2.4) is real but not free. At that matched spread plug w4 also sits about 2–5 δ closer to target (bias −5.0 / −5.6 / −9.1 vs −7.1 / −8.3 / −14.0). It is one seed at n=256.

5. Every discriminating number comes from a review port (RTX 5080, n=256, one seed, q90). None of it comes from the handoff's CPU q50 cells, so it is preliminary evidence, not a reported result.

Evidence files: scratchpad/bdg/defend/mode_split.txt and controls.txt; BDG_HANDOFF.md §1 lines 15-18, §3 lines 94-107, §6.3 lines 221-229, §9.2 lines 276-278.
