objection.title: The stability and fixed-point claims are wrong: V* = tau^2(1-1/eta), not tau^2, and eta=1 cannot widen
objection.argument: 'V_b does not vanish, so the fixed point is stable' is a non-sequitur. Stability needs a gain bound (kappa < 1/(eta-1), plus a transient bound kappa < 2/w_eff(u0), with divergence at 0.154), needs eta > 1, and needs bounded estimator noise; the handoff states none of these. The interior equilibrium is V* = tau^2(1-1/eta), verified to ~1e-15, so at eta=4 the requested sd is undershot by 13.4%. That explains §9.6's 'unexplained' alpha 0.84-0.87 as sqrt(0.75). The runs never reach V* in 50 steps (V_b/tau^2 1.27-1.68 against 0.75), so tau acts as an initial gain rather than a setpoint. At eta=1, w_eff >= 0 and V* = 0 (asked to widen 4x, V falls from 1.0 to 0.062). The bound that actually licenses dropping the clamp is algebraic: V_b >= 0 gives e >= -1, so w_eff >= 1-eta. The handoff omits it.

defence.argument:
PARTIAL. I concede the algebra unreservedly and rebut the severity on five counts. Nothing in the objection changes a single measured number in the handoff; it corrects one bad sentence, supplies a design constraint the spec was missing, and — read one step further than the objection reads it — converts §9.6 from an unexplained defect into a validated closed-form prediction.

WHAT I CONCEDE OUTRIGHT
(1) V* = tau^2(1-1/eta). I reproduced it independently, iterating to convergence from both directions (u0 = 4.0 and 0.05) at eta = 1.5/2/4/8/16: max error 2.7e-15. The equilibrium condition is w_eff = 0, not e = 0. The handoff is wrong to imply tau is the stationary spread.
(2) §2's "V_b does not vanish, so the fixed point is stable and the clamp comes off" is a non-sequitur and must be deleted. Non-vanishing of the signal says nothing about the loop.
(3) eta > 1 is a necessary design constraint (min w_eff = 1-eta), and it is nowhere in §2. Every §4.4 ablation row must carry its eta. This is the most useful thing the objection produces.
(4) §8's ownership claim (b), "the stability argument that licenses removing it", is not valid as worded and must be rewritten into something smaller. That weakens §8.

WHERE THE OBJECTION OVER-REACHES

R1 — the two headline charges are mutually exclusive as criticisms of the same numbers. "At eta=4 the requested sd is undershot by 13.4%" is a statement about an asymptote; the objection itself establishes the runs never approach it (V_b/tau^2 = 1.27-1.68 against 0.75). I reproduced the ladder with the fitted gains: at tau_mult = 0.5 the 50-step window ends at u = 2.07 (mu) / 1.72 (alpha) / 2.68 (gap) against u* = 0.75 — not one §6.1 cell is within a factor of two of the equilibrium. So the 13.4% undershoot describes zero reported cells. It describes only the separate bdg_hold fixed-point cells, which §9.6 already lists as a known defect. The objection cannot bank both charges at once.

R2 — the correction cannot damage the headline claim, because it is a single constant. sd* = tau*sqrt(1-1/eta) is one multiplicative factor, identical across properties and independent of the data at fixed eta: 0.8660 for mu, alpha and gap alike at eta=4. The §6.1 result is *monotone requested-to-achieved on 6/6 curves*, and a positive constant cannot break a monotone map; tau stays invertible (tau_needed = sd_wanted / sqrt(1-1/eta)). The direction label also survives: at tau_mult = 1.5, eta = 4, the equilibrium is sd*/s = 1.299, i.e. the asymptote widens by 30%, *more* than the measured 1.168x. The 13.4% is an undershoot of tau, not of widening. What is wrong is §2's units sentence ("tau_mult reads as a fraction of the natural spread"), not any measurement.

R3 — "eta=1 → V*=0 → unconditional contractor" is the §3 reduction at eta=1, not a new pathology, and it is milder than plug. In the same model at the same fitted gains, over the 50 steps BDG actually runs, from u0 = 0.25 ("asked to widen 4x"): eta=1 gives sd ratio 0.9951/0.9902/0.9855 at wa = 0.10/0.20/0.30, while plug (eta=0) gives 0.9804/0.9611/0.9422. eta=1 contracts *less* than the project's own base arm. The collapse the objection exhibits (V 1.0 → 0.062) needs ~100x more steps than any cell runs — I get u(5000) = 0.063 at wa=0.30 and u(50) = 0.243. Plug has V* = 0 in this model too, and reaches it faster (2.0e-9 vs 4.8e-2 at 5000 steps). So "unconditional contractor whose setpoint is total batch collapse" is asymptotically true and operationally empty; and every eta=1 number in the handoff sits in open item 1, which the handoff already withdraws as a maximum over ~13 cells (independently z = 1.38/1.04, Sidak p = 0.68/0.88).

R4 — on the clamp, the objection's bound reaches the handoff's conclusion and misses half the argument. The real disanalogy is functional form, which I checked against this repo's code: btvg's coefficient is -0.5(1/tau^2 - 1/V_safe) (proj1/src/guidance.py:1494), *reciprocal* in the measured variance, hence a pole — I get +4.95e1, +5.0e3, +5.0e7, +5.0e11 at V = 1e-2, 1e-4, 1e-8, 1e-12, which is the runaway the code comment records (+5.3, +110.8, +78.6). BDG's e is *affine* in it, so e >= -1 and w_eff >= 1-eta for any batch, pole-free. That licenses removing the clamp with no dynamics — the objection is right, and it is a strengthening. But "V_b does not vanish" answers a second question the algebra does not touch: whether the setpoint is *trackable*. The repo's own comment states V_F < tau^2 "eventually happens on EVERY trajectory regardless of the batch", and VARIANCE_DECOMPOSITION.md measures within-trajectory variance ending at 0.0-0.2% of terminal variance while across-batch carries all of it. A servo aimed at a quantity that goes to 0 by construction has no operating regime, clamp or no clamp. There are two true claims welded into one bad sentence; the fix is to split them, not to delete the premise.

R5 — the conclusion the sentence was there to support holds with two orders of magnitude of margin. Using the objection's own bounds and calibration: transient bound 2/w_eff(u0) = 0.1538 at the tau_mult=0.5 start, kappa_peak = 2e-3/3e-3/1e-3, giving margins 76.9x/51.3x/153.8x and first binding near w = 308/205/615. The runs used w=4. 64 independent cells on a different device, batch and seed produced 0 non-finite samples with min w_eff = -2.639, inside the algebraic bound 1-eta = -3. So: wrong argument, right conclusion, large margin. Forward risk worth flagging honestly — the v2 protocol says to extend the strength grid past w=4; at w=16 the margin is still 13-29x, so a one-line runtime assertion covers it rather than a redesign.

THE DEFENCE LINE THE OBJECTION MISSED
It uses u* = 1-1/eta to explain one of §9.6's three values (alpha 0.84-0.87 = sqrt(0.75)) and files mu and gap under "negative natural drift". But §9.6 also says the fixed point is eta-dependent — i.e. the 6-cell hold array swept eta. Inverting eta = 1/(1-(sd*/tau)^2) on all five reported values gives 1.49 / 1.85 / 3.40 / 4.11 / 1.83, clustering on {1.5, 2, 3-4}, with residuals against round-grid sqrt(1-1/eta) of -0.003 / -0.029 / +0.024 / +0.004 / -0.034 — all within 0.034, four of five negative, exactly the uniform small shortfall a finite window plus negative drift gives. Caveat stated plainly: the handoff never defines BDG_FIXED_POINT's units, so sd*/tau is my assumed reading, and five points against a six-value grid is weak on its own. The filename check settles it for free. If it holds, the objection's own correction explains all of §9.6 and open item 6 stops being a defect.

NET: one sentence deleted, one design constraint added, one calibration constant stated, §8(b) shrunk, §9.6 upgraded. Zero cells change. The validity of the method and of every number in §6.1 survives.

TWO EDITS. Both are in docs/methods/BDG_HANDOFF.md.

(A) §2 — delete the sentence "`V_b` does not vanish, so the fixed point is stable and the clamp comes off. **That is what buys the widening direction.**" and replace the "**No clamp.**" paragraph's tail with:

"Two separate facts license removing the clamp, and they answer different questions.
(i) **Boundedness** — no dynamics needed. The error enters *affinely* in the measured variance: `e = V_b/tau^2 - 1` with `V_b >= 0`, so `e >= -1` and `w_eff = 1 + eta*e >= 1 - eta` for any batch whatsoever. `btvg`'s coefficient `-0.5*(1/tau^2 - 1/V_F)` is *reciprocal* in its measured variance and therefore has a pole: `+4.9e1, +5.0e3, +5.0e7, +5.0e11` at `V_F = 1e-2, 1e-4, 1e-8, 1e-12`, which is the measured runaway (`+5.3, +110.8, +78.6`). The widening branch is safe here because it is bounded by the gain, not because the loop is well behaved.
(ii) **Trackability** — `V_F` goes to 0 on every trajectory by construction (`k = (1-t)^2/t` falls ~780x over `t` in [0.5, 0.975]), so `V_F < tau^2` eventually holds regardless of the batch and the setpoint has no operating regime. `V_b` does not vanish — across-batch variance carries essentially all terminal variance while within-trajectory variance ends at 0.0-0.2% of it (`docs/results/VARIANCE_DECOMPOSITION.md`) — so a setpoint on `V_b` is a quantity a loop can actually hold.
Loop **stability** is a third question with its own conditions: `eta > 1` for `V_b = 0` to be repelling, and a gain bound `kappa < 2/w_eff(u_0)` on the transient (`kappa < 1/(eta-1)` asymptotically). At these runs' gains (`kappa_peak` 1e-3 to 3e-3) the transient bound 0.154 is 50-150x away and would first bind near `w ~ 200-600`; the runs used `w = 4`. Assert `kappa*w_eff < 2` at runtime before extending the strength grid.

**Design constraint: `eta > 1`.** `min w_eff = 1 - eta`, so at `eta <= 1` the widening branch does not exist: such cells are `plug` at a variance-modulated positive weight. Label every ablation row with its `eta`.

**Setpoint calibration.** The interior equilibrium is `w_eff = 0`, not `e = 0`, so the stationary spread is `sd* = tau*sqrt(1 - 1/eta)` — `0.866*tau` at `eta = 4`, not `tau`. `tau` is a calibrated monotone handle, not a literal target; invert it as `tau = sd_wanted / sqrt(1 - 1/eta)`. The correction is a single constant at fixed `eta`, identical for all three properties, so the monotone requested-to-achieved result is unaffected. The 50-step guided window does not reach this equilibrium in any case (`V_b/tau^2` runs 1.27-1.68 where the asymptote is 0.75), so in the reported cells `tau` acts as an initial gain; every `sd/unguided` number in §6.1 is measured, not requested."

(B) §8 "What is ours" — replace bullet "the stability argument that licenses removing it (the clamp is only necessary for the vanishing per-sample `V_F`, not for `V_b`)" with:

"the observation that the clamp is an artifact of `btvg`'s *functional form* rather than of variance control — an error affine in the measured variance is bounded by its gain (`w_eff >= 1 - eta`) where `btvg`'s reciprocal one has a pole — together with the separate observation that a setpoint on `V_b` is trackable where one on `V_F` is not, since `V_F` vanishes by construction. This is an algebraic bound plus a measurement, not a stability theorem; do not lean on it."

Also: §9.6 becomes "BDG_FIXED_POINT was estimated from cells whose own widening inflated `V_b`. The correct value is closed-form, `sd*/tau = sqrt(1 - 1/eta)`, which *predicts* the `eta`-dependence measured here rather than contradicting the planner comment." And §6.1/§4.4 table rows gain an `eta` column.

ruling.rationale:
RULING: the objection stands in full on the merits. Every one of its algebraic claims is independently confirmed by two lenses that did not share code (math#7, math#8, math#9, math#10; gpu#13, gpu#14) and is then conceded outright by the defence. The handoff's §2 sentence "V_b does not vanish, so the fixed point is stable and the clamp comes off. That is what buys the widening direction." is a non-sequitur and is also factually wrong about the fixed point: the equilibrium condition is w_eff = 0, not e = 0, so V* = tau^2(1-1/eta) and sd* = tau*sqrt(1-1/eta) (three independent reproductions to 1.9e-15, 2.7e-15 and 5 decimals, from both directions, eta in 1.5-16). eta > 1 is a necessary condition for the widening branch to exist at all (min w_eff = 1-eta) and appears nowhere in §2. Stability requires a gain bound the handoff never states. I verified the two repo facts both sides lean on: proj1/src/guidance.py:1494 is b = (-0.5*(1.0/tau_t**2 - 1.0/V_safe)).clamp(max=0.0), reciprocal in the measured variance, with the comment block at 1478-1493 already stating V_F -> 0 by construction; so the objection's algebraic bound (V_b >= 0 => e >= -1 => w_eff >= 1-eta, pole-free) is the correct licence for dropping the clamp and the handoff omits it.

A conceded claim cannot be defended, so the five rebuttals are severity arguments, and I rule on them as such. Three succeed and should shape the remedy rather than block it. R1/R2: the 13.4% undershoot is an asymptote the 50-step window never approaches (V_b/tau^2 runs 1.27-1.68 against 0.75, math#7, gpu#13, math#10), the correction is a single constant identical across properties at fixed eta, and tau stays invertible — so no §6.1 sd/unguided number changes and the monotone 6/6 result survives. That part of the objection over-reaches and I do not let it touch the measurements. R3: in-window, eta=1 contracts less than plug (0.995/0.990/0.986 vs 0.980/0.961/0.942), and plug shares V* = 0, so "setpoint is total batch collapse" is asymptotically true and operationally empty. R4 is half right and the better half is the defence's: trackability is a genuinely separate question from boundedness, and it is supported in this repo (docs/results/VARIANCE_DECOMPOSITION.md: within-trajectory variance ends at 0.0-0.2% of terminal, across carries all of it, data#10).

Two defence moves I reject as written. (1) The §9.6 upgrade. Inverting eta from five numbers whose units the handoff never defines is a hypothesis, not a validated law; the math lens rates even the alpha match "suggestive, not proof", and five points against a six-value grid with a free scale is weak. §9.6 may not be rewritten as "not a defect" ahead of the check. (2) R5's margins are about 2x optimistic. The transient bound must be evaluated at the per-step peak w_eff, which was measured at +10.354 (gpu#15), not at a run-mean or a 13.0 assumption; the conservative figures are kappa < ~0.113, margin 38-113x, first binding near w ~ 150-450 (math#7 f_basin diverged at kappa = 0.1538 from u0 = 5.16, math#10). The conclusion (safe at w=4, assert before extending the grid) holds either way, which is why this is an amendment and not a rejection.

One thing neither side handles: the new §2 text names w_eff = 0 as the equilibrium, and §3's reduction is singular exactly there (y_eff -> 2.5e5 then flips sign as V/tau^2 crosses 0.75, math#4), while at B=512 near the setpoint w_eff = 0 +/- 0.19 with the sign flipping essentially every step (math#15). If the revision lands without that, §2 and §3 contradict each other and the paper acquires a "controller holding its setpoint" sentence that describes sign-randomised guidance at near-zero net weight. Fixing this is part of the required change, not optional polish.

Net effect on the method's validity: the mechanism, the reduction, the pullback-sign argument and every measured cell survive; what fails is one sentence, one missing design constraint, one mis-stated setpoint, and §8's ownership bullet (b). The defence's own accounting is broadly right about scope, and its revision text is accurate where it restates algebra — adopt it with the five amendments below.

If the residuals do not come out small and mostly negative, §9.6 stays listed as a defect.

§8 "What is ours": accept the defence's shrink of bullet (b), and add that the trackability half is not new material either — the V_F -> 0 premise is already written in this repo at guidance.py:1478-1493, so (b) is at most "we took the contrapositive and measured V_b for it; this is an algebraic bound plus a measurement, not a stability theorem". While §8 is open, drop bullet (c) as well: V/tau^2 is already a shipped repo diagnostic (guidance.py:785 and 1502) and setpoint normalisation is textbook proportional control.

The scan also mixed in 216 EDMsecond cells from a different base model.
2. The 1.010x yardstick is noise. My own bootstrap of n=512 sd ratios from 15,000 real unguided samples gives se = 0.066/0.054/0.037 (mu/alpha/gap) and P(ratio > 1.010 | null) = 0.43/0.42/0.39 — a coin flip. I accept this and drop the figure. It cuts both ways: it also eliminates 31 of the objection's own 32 "widen and clear on every seed" keys, and its btvg_var 1.0218x example (z = +0.41).
3. "Widening replicates on all three properties" is overstated. I reproduce the objection's arithmetic exactly: alpha 1.034/1.042 = +0.63/+0.78 se, mu seed 2 = +1.42 se. Per-cell, widening clears the floor only on gap (+2.58/+3.15) and mu seed 1 (+2.54). And the distinctive claim — widening at fixed centring — is indeed unevidenced today, because no BDG cell reports bias/delta.

REBUTTED — the capability claim survives in a narrower form that I verified rather than asserted. The claim was never "the largest sd ratio in the repo"; it is that tau is a KNOB: a requested setpoint mapped monotonically onto achieved spread in BOTH directions without paying for it with a large mean move. I ran that test over every configuration present in both seed trees (332 matched keys):
- Direction. Zero existing arms have a monotone knob spanning both sides of 1.0. rch is monotone INCREASING over its whole w ladder (1.097 -> 2.048): it can only widen, which is exactly the monotone-only class (Variance-Tilted Diffusion) that §8 already distinguishes BDG from. Every arm that tightens monotonically (plug, smg, lgd_mc, tmpd on alpha) is monotone DECREASING and never reaches 1.0. The only blocks that touch both sides (dflow, smg_mean) do so through a turning point in w, so w -> sd is not invertible and no spread can be requested.

ruling.rationale:
The objection is right on the facts, and the defence concedes them correctly. I checked the numbers myself. results/sweep/alpha__rch__q50__w0.05__tmin0.5__residual.json gives sd = sqrt(12.6206^2 - (72.693 - 75.54)^2) = 12.295. Against unguided 8.640 that is 1.423x, with bias -5.91 delta, mol_stab 0.3730 against a floor of 0.3621, 0 non-finite and 494 clipped steps. The seed-2 twin exists. results/sweep_v2_seed2 has no dflow cells, and no lgd_mc cells either. So three sentences are false and must go: "no existing arm here can do [widening] reproducibly", the 1,766-cell / 1.010x sentence, and "widening replicates on all three properties".

The defence's reformulation holds only in part.

(1) The claim that "no existing arm exposes a monotone bidirectional knob" is true only of the w>=0 grid the repo happened to sweep. Plug over signed w is such a knob. The handoff's own §9.2 has plug at negative w widening alpha 1.153x at mol_stab 0.397. math#6 and gpu#3 also show that BDG's widening branch IS plug at negative w_eff, by algebra. On top of that, gpu#12 replays the recorded e-schedule open-loop and lands within noise of the closed loop. The knob is monotone, but it does not separate BDG from plug with a signed weight. Calling tau a "requested setpoint" is also wrong. The fixed point is tau^2(1-1/eta) and is never reached in 50 steps (gpu#13, math#7), so tau works as a gain.

(2) The claim "0 of 332 widen by >=2 se on both seeds, clear the floor AND hold the mean within 2 delta" rests on a se that is too large, and neither side noticed. Both the attack and the defence bootstrap two INDEPENDENT draws. But guided cells and their unguided control share a seed and initial noise: BDG re-runs unguided in every job at batch 512, and the sweep does the same at batch 128. I tested this on the v2 n=5000 sidecars. Per-molecule corr(f_B unguided, f_B guided) is +0.47 to +0.92. The paired bootstrap se of an n=512 sd ratio is about 0.020 for alpha, 0.014-0.026 for gap and 0.024-0.043 for mu. Unpaired it is about 0.043, 0.033 and 0.062, so pairing roughly halves the se. With paired se, alpha rch q50 w=0.01 widens 1.097x / 1.133x (z about 4.9 / 6.6). It clears the floor on both seeds, has 0 non-finite samples, and moves the mean only -1.31 / -1.47 delta, so it passes the defence's own three-part filter. My match found 186 two-seed keys, not 332. That does not matter: the counterexample stands either way.

(3) The same correction cuts in BDG's favour. The attack puts alpha's 1.034 / 1.042 at 0.6 / 0.8 se, and the defence concedes this. With paired se they are roughly 1.7 / 2.1. That makes alpha borderline, not null. Nobody has measured this on BDG's own sidecars, so it has to be recomputed there.

(4) Two parts of the proposed revision are not like-for-like. The "per unit of sd ratio" displacement numbers for BDG (0.9-4.4 delta) come from the n=256 local port, not from BDG's cells. The "0.65 to 1.22" range mixes the port's 1.219 into the range for BDG's own cells.

(5) The monotone-ordering p ~ 4e-19 is real, but it shows the knob is monotone, which nobody disputes. It says nothing about widening, because a monotone ladder can sit entirely below 1.0. Also, the port's q50 and q90 runs share a seed, so the Stouffer pooling is not over independent runs.

(6) "Established on gap" still needs gap seed 2 to clear its floor. The handoff says it fails, but that failure is against the borrowed 0.362 floor. The per-seed floor, 0.9 x that seed's own unguided mol_stab, has to be applied first.

Net: the objection stands on everything it asserts about the handoff's text. The defence's narrowing survives only as "BDG's tau ladder is a monotone spread map that crosses 1.0 on two seeds, and its widening half is plug at negative w_eff". It does not survive as "no existing arm can do this", or as "0 of N hold centring".

REBUTTED 1: 'wrong for seed 2 (floor 0.3322)'. The 0.369140625 figure is also a B200/128 draw from CUDA's Philox generator. BDG's seed-2 run used CPU mt19937 with one batch of 512. By the objection's own sampling.py:603 argument, 0.3691 is exactly as borrowed as 0.4023. Neither is 'seed 2's own'. The five clearly independent unguided draws on these weights are homogeneous: chi2 = 3.51 on 4 df, p = 0.48, and sweep_v2_seed2 is only z = -1.25 from the pool. So the per-seed B200 numbers are two noisy draws from one population, about 0.396-0.397, and seed labels carry no information across pipelines.

ruling.rationale:
I checked the numbers against the repo and the defence outputs. The objection is right that the floor is borrowed and the verdict is overstated. It is wrong on its seed-2 point and on the claim that the row decides §6.2.

Where the objection stands (the defence concedes all four):
1. §5 of docs/methods/BDG_HANDOFF.md (lines ~177-182) bans comparing BDG with results/sweep. §6 (line 193) then uses 0.362109375 without saying where it comes from. That value is 0.9 x 0.40234375. The defence's inventory shows all 33 fixed-target unguided cells at seed 20260921 on B200, batch 128, n=512 have exactly that value. It is the project's FR3a compare floor (FR3A_VS_FR3_COMPARISON.md:245/255/265).
2. The noise is independent. guidance_sweep.py:1135 seeds one torch.Generator per cell on the device, and sampling.py:603-609 draws randn(B,N,3) and randn(B,N,n_types) per batch. So one CPU batch of 512 shares only the seed integer with four CUDA batches of 128.
3. Each BDG job re-runs unguided (§5), so the per-seed own control exists. The project's convention (FULL_RUN_RESULTS.md, section 8) judges a one-seed row against that seed's own unguided.
4. The numbers reproduce. The row is 178/512 = 0.34766, se 0.0210. It is -0.69 se below the 0.3621 floor and -0.45 se below the pooled 0.3571. A fresh control flips it only if that control is at most 0.38628; P = 0.313 under N(0.3968, 0.0216). Calling a -0.69 se miss "FAILS" breaks the project's own rule. The status doc (lines ~1626-1638) says a floor call below 3 sigma is "a rule applied correctly, not a measured finding".

Where the defence holds:
- "Wrong for seed 2 (floor 0.3322)" fails. 0.369140625 is also a B200, batch-128, CUDA draw, just as borrowed as 0.4023. It is not seed 2's own control.
- Neither side noticed that the §6.2 row (sd 0.787) is the SEED-1 entry in §6.1. So the seed-2 floor never applied to it. The "passes at +0.73 se" line in both tables is a category error and must not reach the paper.
- The independent unguided draws are homogeneous: chi2 = 3.51 on 4 df over 5 clean draws, and 8.53 on 11 df over all 12.
- The pairing argument holds up. Break-even rho is 0.447, and under strong guidance rho is 0.12-0.40 (rho_strong.txt). This row runs at w_eff of about 2-13, so its own control is probably the noisier test. The row is a knife-edge under any floor: P(true mean >= 0.3571) = 0.33.
- §6.2's weaker conclusion survives. If the row cleared, 78 vs 58 of 512 gives z = 1.84, one-sided p = 0.033, and Sidak p over 13 cells = 0.35. That is far below the project's z >= 3 bar.

Limits on the defence:
- The claim that the row "sits on plug's own curve" uses plug w=2 from results/sweep, which is B200, batch 128, one draw. That is suggestive, not established.
- The CPU unguided population itself is only indirectly checked. The evidence is the plug w=4 control agreeing at |z| <= 0.67, which is a weak test. So the job's own unguided must still be reported, not replaced by the pooled value.
- What changes is the word "FAILS" and §1's sentence "tightening enough to matter breaks the chemistry floor". Neither holds as a measured finding at n=512.

objection.title: The only floor-clearing wins (eta=1) are selection noise and mechanistically cannot reflect spread control; §9.5 misplaces the statistical threat
objection.argument: The z-scores are 1.38 and 1.04, with Sidak p 0.68/0.88 over 13 cells, both below the expected null maximum of 1.67 and far from the project's z >= 3 Holm bar. Detecting +0.02 needs ~1,900 samples per arm, so a 6-cell seed-2 rerun is underpowered. At eta=1, w_eff >= 0 and V* = 0, so these cells cannot widen, and the cells that 'win' and the cells that widen are disjoint. A replication would show only strength tuning. The coupling design effect is 1.00-1.04 on in_band and 0.22-0.72 on sd, so the real threat is max-over-grid selection. V_b is also noisier than assumed (kurtosis 6.4, relative se 0.103), and near the setpoint w_eff is 0 +/- 0.19 with near-random sign.

defence.argument:
CONCEDED, the main point. The eta=1 cells are not evidence and should not be cited. I reproduced the unpaired z-scores as 1.376 (alpha) and 1.043 (gap). Sidak over 13 cells gives p = 0.68 / 0.88, far from the project's z >= 3 Holm bar. At eta=1, w_eff = 1 + (V_b/tau^2 - 1) = V_b/tau^2 >= 0 exactly, so these cells can only contract. They cannot support the widening headline in §1 or ownership claim (a) in §8.

The within-batch coupling that §9.5 names does not matter for in_band. An analytic bound gives a design effect of <=1.02-1.08 at w_eff 1-2, which agrees with the math lens (1.00-1.04). Scored unpaired, as bdg_table.py does, the proposed 6-cell rerun has only 0.39 (alpha) / 0.27 (gap) power at the observed effect, and less once the winner's curse shrinks the true effect. The alpha level itself is not unusual. Three n=512 draws of plug w=1 alpha q50 on identical weights gave 23, 32 and 35 hits (homogeneity p = 0.25). BDG's 33 against the pooled control gives z = 0.49.

REBUTTED, four parts.

(1) The objection's selection arithmetic and its "~1,900 per arm" both assume independent samples, and the design is the opposite. BDG cells share initial noise with their controls: the handoff's own eta=0 == plug bit-identity at cell level shows this. On 30 BDG-vs-plug-w1 pairs from the GPU lens's 5080 cells, the paired/unpaired variance ratio of the in_band difference is 0.08-0.88 (median 0.48). At q50 it is 0.08-0.38 for alpha (median 0.28) and 0.31-0.61 for gap (median 0.58).
- Alpha: paired z would be about 2.24-2.59, or 1.65 if the eta=1 cell is as far from plug as plug w=4 is. Family-wise p over 13 cells, using the measured correlation between cells, is about 0.055-0.13 (0.38 in the pessimistic case).
- Gap: paired z is 1.27-1.37 and family-wise p is about 0.39-0.44.
So "selection noise" is shown for gap but is still open for alpha. §9.5's conclusion that the printed z-scores are understated is right in direction, but because of pairing, not coupling. Paired, the 80%-power n at the observed alpha effect is about 470-600, so the 6-cell n=512 rerun scored paired has 0.83 power on alpha (still 0.39 on gap).

(2) The null-maximum benchmark of 1.67 is the independent-tests value. With one shared control (Dunnett, rho = 0.5) the expected maximum of 13 is 1.18; with the measured rho = 0.42 it is 1.28. Alpha's 1.38 lies above both (p_max 0.40-0.44). It is still null, but "below the expected null maximum" is wrong as stated.

(3) "Mechanistically cannot reflect spread control / would show only strength tuning" goes too far. The exact identity (error 7.9e-16) is num_i = (y - F_bar) - w_eff(F_i - F_bar). BDG keeps plug's batch-mean-shift gain at 1 and changes only the contraction gain about the batch mean, while plug's strength knob scales both. At eta=1 the contraction gain is V_b/tau^2: stronger than plug when the batch is wider than tau, weaker when it is narrower, and never negative. That is one-sided spread control with a gain that anneals itself. So eta=1 vs plug w=1 on shared noise is a contraction-only contrast, not a strength sweep.
- Empirical support (5080, eta=4, n=256, q90): BDG's tightest setting matches plug w=4's spread contraction (mu 0.825 vs 0.818, gap 0.924 vs 0.929 of plug-w1 sd). It moves the batch mean by -0.07+/-0.36 and -0.20+/-0.20 delta, against plug w=4's +2.64+/-0.53 and +1.68+/-0.25 delta.
- Alpha is the exception (-1.83+/-0.50 delta), the drag math#12 predicted.
- At q50, BDG's target, contraction governs in_band (data lens), so the eta=1 direction starts with a positive prior. Winning cells and widening cells being disjoint is what §1 predicts at q50, not a refutation.

(4) The sign-randomisation and kurtosis-6.4 points do not apply to these cells. At eta=1, w_eff = V_b/tau^2 > 0 always, and its relative jitter is relse(V_b) = 0.076 for alpha (kurtosis 3.93) and 0.053 for gap (kurtosis 2.42). The 0.103 figure is mu's, and mu has no eta=1 win.

On "§9.5 misplaces the threat": the handoff already ranks selection first (§9.1 names the grid-search artifact) and coupling fifth. The ranking is right; only the mechanism in §9.5 is wrong.

Net: the eta=1 cells prove nothing and cannot carry the two-sided claim. They are not shown to be noise for alpha, and they do not reduce to strength tuning.

So eta=1 keeps plug's mean-shift gain at 1 and changes only the contraction gain, while plug's strength knob scales both. That is not the same as a plug strength sweep. It is still not the setpoint spread control the handoff sells, because V* = 0.
- **Estimator noise.** The kurtosis-6.4 figure and the sign-randomisation point belong to mu and to eta=4 near w_eff = 0. They do not apply here. For the eta=1 alpha and gap cells, relse(V_b) is 0.076 and 0.053 (I checked the formula), and w_eff is always positive.

The defence is right that the neglected issue is pairing. eta=0 being bit-identical to plug shows the cells share initial noise, so the unpaired se is the wrong test. objection.title: Claim (a), two-sided control, is occupied by MGD, which the handoff mis-describes as mean-only, and VTD's widening is unacknowledged
objection.argument: MGD (arXiv 2602.17211) drives a sign-free residual between an ensemble moment and a target, including quadratic moments, so it is already a two-sided second-moment controller. §3's 'mean-only' description contradicts the team's own Three_New §5.6. VTD's repulsion of posterior means is structurally BDG's widening branch. Inside the repo, widening is negative-weight plug.

defence.argument:
I concede the core of this objection and rebut two of its sub-claims.

CONCEDED: claim (a) is occupied by MGD. §8 claims "removing the positive-part restriction so one controller both narrows and widens" as ours, and that cannot stand as a mechanism claim. I read MGD's HTML (arXiv 2602.17211v2) myself. Its SDE (Eq. 13) is dX = (eta_t - sigma^2 theta_t)^T grad phi dt + noise. Its corrector (Eq. 25) sets theta from the gap between the ensemble moment of phi and a target m_(t+h), and that gap can have either sign. phi can be quadratic. I then specialised MGD's quadratic corrector to one scalar property, phi = (f, f^2). The per-sample drift becomes -(theta_1 + 2 theta_2 F_i) g_i. That is affine in F_i with coefficients shared across the batch, so it is exactly plug at weight w' = 2 theta_2 aimed at y' = -theta_1/(2 theta_2), to 2.4e-16. Its slope goes negative (widening) whenever the current variance is below the target, in 99.6% of 500 draws. So MGD narrows and widens with the same algebraic structure as BDG.

Line 101 ("spbc/MGD's mean-only corrector") is wrong. The mean-only corrector is spbc's; MGD's corrector is not mean-only. The line also under-states the handoff's own §3 reduction, which covers MGD's full two-sided corrector and not just a mean-only one. Fixing it makes §3 stronger. It is the only place that conflicts with Three_New §5.6.

What MGD does NOT do, per the paper: it is a standalone maximum-entropy sampler with no learned score and no pretrained generator. phi is an explicit function of the current state x, not a learned property predictor applied to the endpoint estimate. m_t is the moment trajectory of the interpolant, not a spread the user asks for. theta comes from a Gram-matrix solve, not a proportional gain. These are differences of setting and instantiation. They give an honest, incremental ownership claim, not a new mechanism.

REBUTTED 1, "VTD's widening is unacknowledged". This is literally false. Line 251 names VTD as prior art for spread targeting through a batch distribution and says it is "monotone, can only widen, on a fixed linear feature". I checked that description against the VTD HTML and it is exact:
- the target is proportional to Var_n^A(x) times the product of p0(x_i);
- there is no strength parameter and no setpoint;
- contraction is not discussed;
- A is linear;
- the interaction term is (2/n) J^T A^T A (mu_i - mu_bar).

What is genuinely missing is one sentence: BDG's dispersion term with e<0 has the same per-sample form as VTD's interaction term, with g_i from a learned f_A in place of A^T A, and with a signed coefficient tied to a setpoint in place of VTD's fixed positive one. That is an addition to the text, not a correction.

REBUTTED 2, "inside the repo, widening is negative-weight plug". This is true only for the deviations; the mean behaves differently. BDG's numerator splits as (y - F_bar) + w_eff (F_bar - F_i), verified to 8e-16. So the push on the batch mean always stays at weight +1 toward y, and only the spread around it is scaled by w_eff. Plug at a negative weight w scales both parts by w, so it pushes the mean away from y.

- Toy check (B=512, heterogeneous gains): at matched terminal sd 1.320, BDG ends with bias -1.088 (plug w=1: -1.135; unguided: -3.041). Constant plug at w=-0.303 ends at -4.153, worse than unguided.
- Real cells from the GPU lens at the q90 target (n=256, one seed): BDG e4t1.5 widens sd to 1.219/1.145/1.129 of unguided. Its bias/delta is -7.010/-13.987/-7.393 against unguided -9.883/-19.203/-10.051. That keeps 157%/77%/95% of plug w=1's bias reduction. The reductions versus unguided are about 4 to 6 se. Plug at a negative w cannot do this by construction.

This also explains §9.2's result without contradicting it. At q50 the batch is already nearly centred (alpha unguided bias +0.55 delta), so pushing the mean away from y costs almost nothing, and negative plug looks competitive. At q90 it should not.

Caveats:
- The mean decoupling is not new either: MGD and Three_New §5.2 solve for the mean and the variance jointly. It defends BDG against the negative-weight-plug reduction only, not against MGD.
- I have not measured negative-weight plug at q90; that is the experiment below.
- Gain heterogeneity adds a mean drag scaled by w_eff (math#12). It is visible on alpha, where bias is -13.99 against plug's -12.42.

ruling.rationale:
I checked the claims against the repo and re-ran the defence script with the repo .venv. It reproduces: the split has error 8.06e-16, the MGD specialisation 2.43e-16 with 99.6% sign agreement, and the toy gives BDG bias -1.088 at sd 1.320 against -4.153 for sd-matched plug at w=-0.303. I also checked scratchpad/bdg/table.txt: the q90 bias/delta and sd numbers the defence quotes are exact.

The objection has three parts, and I rule on each.

1. CORE: claim (a) is occupied by MGD, and line 101 mis-describes MGD. The objection STANDS, and the defence concedes it. Line 101 says "spbc/MGD's mean-only corrector". According to the novelty lens and the defence, who both read the MGD HTML, MGD's corrector is a sign-free residual on ensemble moments that include quadratic ones (Eq. 25). Specialised to phi=(f,f^2), it is affine in F_i with batch-shared coefficients, and it widens when theta_2<0. So "removing the positive-part restriction so one controller both narrows and widens" (line 257) cannot stand as a mechanism claim. Line 101 also clashes with Three_New line 510 ("Moment matching itself is occupied by MGD").

2. "VTD's widening is unacknowledged". OVERSTATED. Lines 250-252 cite VTD as prior art for spread targeting through a batch distribution. The characterisation "monotone, can only widen, on a fixed linear feature" is accurate per the novelty lens (novelty#2). What is missing is narrower: BDG's e<0 dispersion term has the same per-sample form as VTD's interaction term (2/n) J^T A^T A (mu_i - mu_bar). That needs one added sentence, not a correction.

3. "Inside the repo, widening is negative-weight plug". REFUTED as stated. The algebra shows (y-F_i) - eta*e*(F_i-F_bar) = (y-F_bar) + w_eff*(F_bar-F_i). So the drive on the batch mean stays at weight +1 toward y, and only the deviations are scaled by w_eff. "Plug at w_eff<0 aimed at y_eff" is the same statement, because w_eff*(y_eff-F_bar) = y-F_bar. Plain plug at a negative w aimed at y is a different field, and it pushes the mean away from y. §9.2's comparator is that plain plug. The math lens (math#6) and the attack drop the y_eff shift; the gpu lens (gpu#3) keeps it.

The q90 GPU-port cells support the distinction. e4t1.5 has bias/delta -7.01/-13.99/-7.39, against -8.05/-12.42/-7.25 for plug w=1 and -9.88/-19.20/-10.05 for unguided, at sd 1.22/1.15/1.13 of unguided. Those numbers carry several limits:
- one seed, n=256;
- run with a review port rather than the handoff's code;
- alpha keeps only 77% of plug's reduction;
- every q90 guided cell fails the local floor (0.3902).

Negative plug at q90 has not been measured. The algebra predicts it will pull the mean away from y, but the clip and the nonlinear f could weaken that.

The defence is also right that decoupling the mean is not new either: MGD and Three_New §5.2 solve for the mean and the variance jointly. So this defends BDG against being reduced to negative-weight plug. It does not rescue claim (a).

objection.title: Claims (b) and (c) are already in the repo's code, and (b)'s argument is the wrong one
objection.argument: (b) restates the comment above btvg's clamp (guidance.py ~1478-1494), including the same +5.3/+110.8/+78.6 figures. The correct reason, w_eff >= 1-eta, is not given. (c) V/tau^2 is already persisted as btvg2_V_over_tau2 (guidance.py:785, :1502), and it is ordinary proportional control. The controller framing is oversold because the setpoint is never reached.

defence.argument:
I CONCEDE the novelty charge against (c), and the attribution charge against (b). I REBUT the claim that the handoff gives "the wrong argument" and that w_eff >= 1-eta is "the correct reason". I PARTLY concede the charge that the controller framing is oversold.

1. (b) attribution. CONCEDED. The reason btvg needs the clamp, and the figures +5.3/+110.8/+78.6, come verbatim from the comment at guidance.py:1480-1494. §2 cites that location (as :1471, a 23-line drift in the author's tree). §8(b) then lists the whole parenthetical as "ours". Only the transfer to V_b is new.

2. "The correct reason is w_eff >= 1-eta". REBUTTED as a replacement; ACCEPTED as a missing half. The bound cannot be what makes BDG safe, because an unsafe law satisfies it just as well. I fed BDG's own bounded error law e = S/tau^2 - 1 the two candidate statistics:
- Fed btvg's V_F: on the repo's measured curves e ends at -0.992 to -1.000 in 3/3 runs. That is pinned at the bound, i.e. maximum widening. It holds for every request above 0.9-4.5% of the natural spread, and even a TIGHTEN request gets the widening sign on 42-66% of the window.
- Fed V_b: a tighten request never gets the widening sign (0%), a widen request always does (100%), and at tau_mult 1 the sign alternates. So the sign follows the batch and the request, not t.
- In the dynamic toy, w_eff bottoms at exactly -3.00 = 1-eta for the V_F-fed law, yet it widens on 68-94% of steps under tighten or neutral requests. It overshoots a neutral request by +39% (k0=0.01) to 4.95x (k0=0.05) and diverges under constant gain. The V_b loop converges to tau*sqrt(1-1/eta) to 4 dp.

btvg's defect is that its sign is unconditional ("regardless of the batch"). The size of its coefficient only made that worse. So the handoff's "V_b does not vanish" is the load-bearing premise, meaning V_b is not scheduled to zero. What it lacks is:
- the sign-consistency of the actuator (math#11: the pulled-back push is c_i|J_i^T g_i|^2, so dV_b has sign -sign(e) for any J);
- the widening bound (gpu#14);
- the fact that the TIGHTENING side is unbounded (e = +184 to +1074 if tau were set at btvg's band width), so the gain bound kappa < 2/w_eff(V0) and eta > 1 are still needed (math#7).

Its words "the fixed point is stable" are wrong. The fixed point is tau^2(1-1/eta) (math#8, gpu#13), and I concede that.

3. (c). CONCEDED, and more than the objection says. V/tau^2 is not only a persisted diagnostic (785, 1502). It is already the argument of btvg's control law (1494: -(1/2tau^2)(1-1/r)) and of btvg2's (733: (0.5/s^2)(1-1/r)_+). btvg2's law is already in plug units, which is why guidance_sweep.py:352-354 exempts it from strength_scale, and its dV is already the signed-deviation gradient of a sample variance (728-729). The only formal difference in the error law is that BDG is linear in r and therefore bounded when widening: at r=1e-4 the widening coefficient is +4 for bdg against +5000 for btvg/btvg2. That difference belongs inside (b). P-control is the right description and is textbook.

4. Controller framing. PARTIAL.
- True: the setpoint is not reached. In 12/12 per-step GPU logs the achieved sd/s is 0.69-0.76, 0.93-1.03 and 1.02-1.25 for requests of 0.5, 1 and 1.5.
- But the handoff never claims the setpoint is reached. §3 already forbids "variance control", and §1 claims only a monotone requested-to-achieved mapping, which gpu#7 replicated 6/6.
- The miss is what a finite-gain P-controller does. It has a closed-form droop, V* = tau^2(1-1/eta), and two further limits:
  - Actuator fade: (1-t)/t goes to 0. At tau_mult 0.5, V/tau^2 is still rising by +0.024 to +0.052 per step over the last 10 steps, despite w_eff +3.6 to +4.5.
  - The clip binds.
- Only 4/12 cells are stationary (|slope| <= 0.0022 per step), and they sit at a point shifted by droop and drift.
- The objection cannot have it both ways: a loop cannot be both "ordinary proportional control" and "not a controller".
- The honest wording is "a spread request with a measured calibration curve", not "a setpoint".

defence.proposed_revision:
§2, replace lines 72-77 ("**No clamp.** ... That is what buys the widening direction.") with:

"**No clamp.** `btvg` clamps its variance coefficient at `<= 0` (guidance.py:1494). The reason, and the measured runaway (+5.3, +110.8, +78.6), are in the comment there and are not ours. Two facts together license removing the clamp for `V_b`, and neither is enough alone.
(1) *Closure.* The dispersion push moves `V_b` with sign `-sign(e)` for every molecule, because the pulled-back push is `c_i |J_i^T g_i|^2`, a squared norm. And `V_b` is not scheduled to zero: `across(t)` settles within 5% of the terminal variance (docs/results/VARIANCE_DECOMPOSITION.md). `V_F` instead falls 15,870-35,534x on the schedule whatever the batch does. So any two-sided law on `V_F`, even this bounded one, ends every run at `e ~ -1`, maximum widening, whatever spread was requested.
(2) *Bounded widening.* `V_b >= 0` gives `e >= -1`, so the widening coefficient is at most `eta` and `w_eff >= 1 - eta`. `btvg`'s `(1/r - 1)/2` is unbounded (+5000 at r = 1e-4). Boundedness alone is not safe: a bounded law on `V_F` still widens unconditionally and diverges under sustained gain.
The tightening side is NOT bounded (`e` can reach `V_b/tau^2`). The step therefore still needs `kappa < 2/w_eff(V_0)`, and `eta > 1` is needed for `V = 0` to be repelling. The loop is a proportional controller whose equilibrium is `V_b* = tau^2 (1 - 1/eta)` (droop), not `tau^2`. This is also the closed form behind §9.6."

§8, replace lines 257-260 ("**What is ours:** ... does not reduce to any fixed weight schedule.") with:

"**What is ours (narrow):** we apply the repo's existing setpoint-relative variance law to the across-batch dispersion `V_b` with the positive part removed. `btvg` and `btvg2` already use a function of `V/tau^2` in their control laws, and Three_New §5.2 already specifies the one-sided version on the batch forecast variance. We add the argument for why removing the clamp is safe for `V_b` and not for `V_F`: closure plus a widening coefficient bounded by `eta` (§2). It is ordinary proportional control with a known droop. `tau` is a spread *request* with a measured monotone calibration curve (achieved sd/s 0.69-0.76 / 0.93-1.03 / 1.02-1.25 at tau_mult 0.5 / 1 / 1.5, GPU replication n=256), not a setpoint the loop reaches in the 50-step window. The setpoint-relative error `e` is not claimed. (The fixed-schedule claim is addressed separately.)"

In §1 line 17, change "compare it to a requested setpoint" to "compare it to a requested spread".

ruling.rationale:
I verified both attribution charges directly in the repo, so they do not rest on either side's scripts.

(b) ATTRIBUTION — OBJECTION STANDS (conceded, and confirmed). proj1/src/guidance.py:1480-1487 already contains the whole argument and all three figures: "V_F is a per-sample posterior variance and goes to 0 as t -> 1 by construction (k = (1-t)^2/t falls by ~780x over t in [0.5, 0.975]), while tau^2 is a population band half-width. So V_F < tau^2 eventually happens on EVERY trajectory regardless of the batch, and without this clamp the sign flip turns the last ~15% of every run into active widening (measured b = +5.3, +110.8, +78.6)." Handoff §2 lines 72-77 restate that; §8 line 258 lists it as ours. Mitigation: §2 does point at the file, so this is under-attribution rather than undisclosed appropriation — and the pointer is stale (:1471 is `V_ok = V > 0`; the clamp is :1494).

(c) — OBJECTION STANDS, and is understated. V/tau^2 is not merely a persisted diagnostic (:785, :1502). It is the argument of btvg's own law (:1494, b = -0.5(1/tau^2 - 1/V_safe)) and of btvg2's (:733, 0.5/s^2 (1 - tau2/V_safe)_+); btvg2 is already in plug units (guidance_sweep.py strength_scale exempts it by prefix); and Three_New §5.2 already defines V as the batch variance of terminal forecasts z_i with b_V = -eta_V (V - tau^2)_+ against a setpoint tau. That is BDG's V_b, one-sided. Claim (c) must be dropped, not defended.

"THE CORRECT REASON IS w_eff >= 1-eta" — DOES NOT STAND as a replacement. e = V/tau^2 - 1 >= -1 holds for any nonnegative variance, V_F included (after the 1e-12 clamp the code already applies), so the bound cannot separate a safe law from an unsafe one: a bounded two-sided law driven by V_F still ends every run at e ~ -1, maximum widening, because V_F is scheduled to zero. That premise is repo-verified independently of the defence's toys — VARIANCE_DECOMPOSITION.md has within(t) falling 15,870-35,534x to 0.0-0.2% of terminal variance while across(t) settles within 5% of it. So closure is load-bearing and the bound is a necessary second half; neither suffices alone, since the gain bound kappa < 2/w_eff(V_0) and eta > 1 are still required.

What is genuinely wrong in §2 is the inference, not the topic: "so the fixed point is stable" is false — the interior equilibrium is w_eff = 0, i.e. V_b* = tau^2(1-1/eta). The defence concedes this.

CONTROLLER FRAMING — the defence's rhetorical move fails, its substance holds. "Ordinary proportional control" and "the setpoint is never reached" are the same statement, not a contradiction: finite-gain P-control has droop by construction, so the objection can have it both ways. But the attack's conclusion ("not a controller") overshoots; the fix is the word. "Setpoint" must go from §1 line 17 and everywhere else. Droop is also not the whole miss: run-mean V_b/tau^2 is 1.27-1.68 at tau_mult 0.5 against an asymptote of 0.75, so the loop is nowhere near equilibrium in 50 steps; actuator fade ((1-t)/t -> 0) and the velocity clip bind too, and near equilibrium w_eff is 0 +/- 0.19 at B=512 with its sign flipping most steps. The part that replicated independently is the monotone requested-to-achieved mapping (6/6 curves, different device, batch, n, seed).

The proposed revision is close to right; four places overclaim or mis-state (items 1f, 1g, 5, 6 below). The proposed droop-precompensation run cannot rescue (b) or (c) and must not be sold as a novelty defence.

defence.argument:
I concede most of this objection. I push back on two points: one piece of the objection goes too far, and one is imprecise.

CONCEDED.
(1) §8 has to cite the closed-loop guidance literature. §3's line "What does NOT reduce: the feedback" and §8(d) both frame BDG as closed-loop versus open-loop. Feedback Guidance (2506.06085) already makes that argument about CFG. §8(c), the setpoint-relative error e, is textbook proportional control, and CFG-Ctrl (2603.03281) makes that explicit. The repo already knew this category was taken: Three_New line 24 lists "optimal-control guidance" as occupied, and TOCFlow, Jeffrey guidance, HIG and Multilevel-SMC sit in Three_New's §8 prior-art table (lines 939-944). Listing adaptive scales only as "autoguidance, CFG++, guidance intervals" undersells a literature that is explicitly control-theoretic.
(2) §8 understates how much of BDG the team's own §5.2-5.3 already contains:
- the same statistic, V_b (Three_New line 379: z_i is the f_A forecast);
- the setpoint τ;
- the gradient ΔV = (2/B)Σ c_i ν_i (line 390), which is §2's derivation;
- the closed-loop moment ODE (line 439);
- an allocation that is affine in F_i. I reproduced this to 1.5e-15, so §3's reduction applies to §5.2 as well.
"Abandoned in its own revision" (handoff line 255) is also inaccurate. Line 373 says the controller was kept as an optional comparison.
(3) The ~0.85 / ~0.1 figures have no artifact. A grep over every .md, .py, .txt and .slurm file outside the worktrees finds "bdg" only in the handoff itself. The novelty lens, working independently with a stated scope, also arrived at 0.85 for a course project, but that is a replacement estimate, not the missing checks.

REBUTTED: the claim that these papers occupy "batch-feedback-adaptive guidance weight". I read all three abstracts directly. All three feed back a per-sample signal:
- FBG: "a state-dependent coefficient", applied "whether a particular sample needs correction".
- SOC (2505.19367): strength "selected based on time, the current sample, and the conditioning class".
- CFG-Ctrl: "conditional-unconditional discrepancy as an error signal".
None of them feeds back a cross-sample statistic, and none sets a target for a distributional quantity. 2501.14822 sets ensemble variance by choosing the DDIM step count, calibrated offline. It is open-loop and has no guidance term. These papers do occupy "feedback-adaptive guidance weight" and the closed-loop framing, and that is why they must be cited. The batch ingredient is occupied by MGD, VTD and Particle Guidance, and MGD itself is maximum-entropy sampling from prescribed moments, not steering a pretrained generator toward a property value. So the novelty lens's rating of the combination as "narrow and unclaimed" (novelty#9) still stands.

SHARPENED: "the real delta is deleting (.)_+ and using a scalar gain" is nearly right but misses the part that matters. There is an exact identity, holding to 2.9e-15 over 2000 random batches:
- BDG = (y−F̄) − (η/τ²)(V − τ²(1−1/η)) c_i
- §5.2 with (.)_+ deleted, equal mobility = η_μ(y−F̄) − (η_V/(2V))(V − τ²) c_i

The only substantive difference is the normaliser: BDG divides by the constant setpoint τ², §5.2 by the measured V. The rest is a relabelled setpoint. That normaliser is the whole reason the two-sided version is safe:
- §5.2 without the clamp has exactly btvg's (V−τ²)/V gain; the ratio to guidance.py:1494's raw coefficient is 2.0 at every V. Its widening gain diverges as V→0: +1e8 at V/τ² = 1e-8. Its per-sample edit is 1.86e3 at V/τ² = 1e-6.
- BDG's widening gain is bounded by η−1 = 3, because V_b ≥ 0 forces e ≥ −1. Its edit at V/τ² = 1e-6 is 0.011.

So deleting (.)_+ from §5.2 as written would not be licensed by the argument that forced btvg's clamp. BDG's normalisation is what makes it unconditionally bounded (gpu#14). An honest twist: the handoff's stated licence, "V_b does not vanish", is the argument §5.2-two-sided would need. BDG itself does not need it.

The normaliser has two measured costs:
- The fixed point is τ²(1−1/η) = 0.75τ² at η=4, against §5.2's exact τ² (simulated: 0.75000 vs 1.00000).
- There is no mobility-weighted mean correction. When mobility correlates with deviation at 0.93, §5.2's 2x2 solve moves the batch mean by exactly the requested +0.300, while BDG's mean moves −1.786 (math#12).

Net novelty: one design decision relative to the team's own spec (one benefit, two costs), plus an implementation §5.2 never had. That implementation is a per-step term sharing plug's single VJP, costs zero extra NFE, and was ported from the prose in 610 lines (gpu#20). This is incremental. It is defensible for a course project only if §8 is rewritten to say exactly this. The workshop figure (0.1 in the handoff, 0.05 from the novelty lens) is too low to change any decision and should simply be dropped.

"## 8. Novelty — the honest position

**Not new (cite all of these).**
- *State-feedback guidance weight*: Feedback Guidance (arXiv 2506.06085) treats CFG as an open-loop controller and makes its coefficient state-dependent. Adaptive Guidance via SOC (2505.19367) chooses the strength from time, sample and condition. CFG-Ctrl (2603.03281) casts CFG as proportional control with a Lyapunov-stable replacement. Because V_b ≥ 0 forces e ≥ −1, the widening coefficient is bounded by η−1 for every batch. §5.2 with the clamp deleted would instead inherit btvg's (V−τ²)/V gain, which diverges as V→0. ruling.rationale:
I checked all three charges against the repo, and all three stand. The defence concedes each of them.

(1) Missing closed-loop literature. The handoff's §8 (lines 249-253) lists adaptive scales only as "autoguidance, CFG++, guidance intervals". A grep of docs/ finds 2506.06085, 2505.19367, 2603.03281 and 2501.14822 nowhere, yet §3 ("What does NOT reduce: the feedback") and §8(d) argue open-loop versus closed-loop. I fetched the FBG abstract myself: a "state-dependent coefficient to self-regulate guidance amounts", which is exactly that framing. The repo already treated the category as occupied: Three_New line 24 lists "optimal-control guidance", and lines 939-944 log TOCFlow, Jeffrey guidance, HIG and Multilevel-SMC. §8 cites none of these.

(2) §8 understates Three_New §5.2-5.3. Lines 379-390 define V as the batch variance of the forecast z_i (BDG's V_b), with the setpoint tau and ΔV=(2/B)Σc_iν_i. Line 439 holds the closed-loop ODE. The defence's script output (s52_vs_bdg.json) confirms the §5.2 allocation is affine in F_i with batch-shared coefficients (rel err 1.5e-15). §3's reduction therefore covers §5.2 too, and cannot separate BDG from it. "Abandoned in its own revision" (line 255) is imprecise: line 373 retains the controller as an optional comparison, and line 402 only demotes it from being the default.

(3) The ~0.85 / ~0.1 figures have no artifact. My grep for "bdg" over the .md/.py/.txt/.slurm/.sh files outside the worktrees returns only BDG_HANDOFF.md. "Slightly novel" and "yes / yes" appear only at lines 265-266.

Where the defence wins: its rebuttal of one sub-claim succeeds. The attack said FBG, SOC and CFG-Ctrl occupy "batch-feedback-adaptive guidance weight". I fetched the abstracts: FBG is per-sample. 2501.14822 controls variance "by varying the number of diffusion steps", which is open-loop with no guidance term. MGD "samples maximum entropy distributions" from prescribed moments; it does not steer a pretrained generator toward a property value. So these papers occupy "feedback-adaptive weight" and the closed-loop framing, and MGD, VTD and Particle Guidance occupy the batch ingredient. The intersection remains narrow and unclaimed, which matches novelty#9's own rating. The attack's phrase overreaches, but that does not reduce what must change.

The defence's sharpening is correct and should be adopted. The identity BDG num_i = (y−F̄) − (η/τ²)(V − τ²(1−1/η))c_i holds (2.9e-15), and I confirmed it by hand: 1+ηe = (η/τ²)(V − τ²(1−1/η)). The gain table in S3 shows that §5.2 with the clamp deleted has btvg's divergent (τ²−V)/V gain: 1e8 at V/τ²=1e-8, exactly 2x btvg's raw coefficient. BDG's widening coefficient is capped at η−1. Setting the correct fixed point, τ²(1−1/η), aside, the delta from the team's own spec is therefore one normalisation choice with one benefit and two measured costs. The costs are the fixed-point undershoot (S4, which math#7 and gpu#13 corroborate) and the uncorrected mean drag (S6, math#12). These are refinements of the objection's "real delta", not a defence against it.

Two parts of the proposed text are themselves defective:
(a) "This choice is what makes the two-sided version safe" overstates it. The η−1 bound is unconditional (gpu#14), but loop stability also needs η>1 and a gain bound: asymptotic κ<1/(η−1), transient κ<2/w_eff(u0) (math#7). It also omits that the widening branch runs at w_eff<0, i.e. negative-weight plug (math#6, gpu#3).
(b) The replacement sentence for lines 265-266 cites a BDG row in INNOVATION_IDEAS_INDEX.md §3.2 that does not exist. Adding it now would recreate the untraceable-citation defect this objection is about.

objection.title: No project metric or use case rewards batch-spread control, and there is no single-molecule mode
objection.argument: Under dist, spread scaling buys at most +0.0004 at plug w=4. The binding quantity is corr(F,y). evaluate_samples has no distribution-matching metric, and guided arms are already more diverse than unguided. V_b is 0/0 at B=1, and the method forces batch = n, which conflicts with the batch-128 protocol.

defence.argument:
PARTIAL. The two mechanical sub-claims (no single-molecule mode; the method forces batch = n) are refuted by measurement, and so is the headline ("no project metric rewards batch-spread control"). The dist and diversity sub-claims are conceded outright, and I concede a deeper point the objection did not make.

(1) HEADLINE REFUTED — the project's own metrics do reward spread, and one of them at both targets. `spread = sqrt(RMSE^2 - bias^2)/delta`, "is it concentrated?", is a named column in docs/results/ARM_RANKINGS.md, the project's complete arm-ranking document; `sd/delta` is in the FULL_RUN_V2_RESULTS headline block; and the quantity is recoverable exactly from two shipped fields of evaluate_samples (`prop_rmse_eval`, `f_B_mean`) — the identity the red team itself used to scan 1,766 cells (data#5 validated it to 2.5e-6). More decisively, ARM_RANKINGS.md ranks arms by MAE/delta ("MAE is the primary metric ... band coverage is ... too weak to rank on"), and MAE/delta is strictly monotone decreasing in batch spread on 6/6 property x target curves, at q90 as well as q50. At BDG's own achieved contraction: -25.2/-31.9/-20.7% at q50 and -7.5/-6.4/-1.9% at q90 (ceiling at q90 is (E|r|-|b|)/delta = 12.8/7.9/2.2%). So the objection's "no project metric rewards batch-spread control" is false on the project's primary ranking metric at the project's headline target.

(2) HEADLINE REFUTED AGAIN ON IN_BAND AT BDG'S TARGET. BDG ran at q50 (data#1: chi2 1.4, p=0.96; excluded from q90 at p~4e-4). q50 is not an off-protocol choice: it is the target of ARM_RANKINGS.md and the only protocol where all three external comparators ran (FR3A_VS_FR3_COMPARISON.md:243). Rescoring 15,000 real unguided v2 samples at q50 at BDG's *own achieved* spread ratios (0.739/0.681/0.787 — not the s=0.3 headline the red team quoted), the pure-spread lever buys in_band +0.0295/+0.0225/+0.0296 against +0.0036/-0.0018/+0.0045 for perfectly centring the same samples: 8.2x, infinite (centring is negative), 6.6x. in_band is strictly decreasing in s across BDG's entire reachable range [0.65, 1.17] on all three properties. At q50, spread is not merely rewarded, it is the only lever that pays.

(3) "NO SINGLE-MOLECULE MODE" REFUTED. At B=1, F_i - F_bar = 0 identically, so the dispersion term vanishes whatever e is and BDG is bit-identical to plug: max|num_bdg - num_plug| = 0.000e+00. The 0/0 is in V_b alone, and V_b multiplies a quantity that is exactly zero. B=2 already gives a live controller. So BDG has no single-molecule *capability* (there is no batch dispersion to control) but no single-molecule *failure* either — it degrades to the arm it is built on. One guard line (V_b := 0 for B < 2, and never use the reduced form w_eff*(y_eff - F_i) at B=1, which does NaN) makes that exact. Context: three of evaluate_samples' own metrics (diversity_mean_pairwise, diversity_logdet, uniqueness_of_valid) are undefined at B=1, and no cell in this repo runs below B=128.

(4) "FORCES BATCH = n" REFUTED QUANTITATIVELY — this is the objection's strongest-looking point and it dissolves. The mean-field loop contains no B: the 2/(B-1) is absorbed into eta (math#2) and neither kappa nor w_eff = 1+eta*e depends on B, so B enters only through relse(V_b) = sqrt(2/(B-1)). Measured in the loop model the math lens calibrated to the handoff's own 6.1 ladder (rms 0.04-0.06 over 10 points), 400 replicates: the mean achieved sd/unguided moves at most 0.0071 across B from 32 to 4096 — smaller than the per-run se at B=128 (0.028). Running the protocol's 4x128 instead of 1x512 on the same 512 molecules changes the pooled sd/unguided by 0.03-0.16% (9/9 cells), about 30x below the single-run se. Noise rectification at B=128 is +0.0003 to +0.0008% on sd. So handoff lines 181-182 are over-cautious: the requirement is B >= ~64, not batch == n, and [doable#18]'s item 5 ("cannot be matched without changing the method") is wrong. Batch 128 is in fact *preferable*: n=5000 at batch 128 gives 40 replicate controllers whose between-batch scatter is a free honest error bar on the achieved spread (se 0.0044 vs 0.0136 for one batch of 512, 3.1x tighter) and which breaks the sample coupling behind the handoff's own open item 5. The protocol conflict becomes a footnote and an upgrade.

(5) CONCEDED WITHOUT RESERVATION. Under dist the lever is inert (<=+0.0004 at plug w=4) and the binding quantity is corr(F,y) = 0.13-0.59 -> 0.68-0.80, a per-molecule tracking property no batch-variance setpoint can address; BDG never ran at dist and must not be recast for it. evaluate_samples has no W1/KS/distribution-matching term. Diversity already favours the guided arms, so "restore collapsed diversity" is dead. And at q90 in_band the objection is simply right: the whole spread lever is worth <=+0.005, tightening to BDG's ratios *lowers* in_band (-0.006/-0.010/-0.030), and debiasing buys 10-35x more.

(6) THE CONCESSION THE OBJECTION MISSED, AND IT IS BIGGER. The metrics reward spread control; BDG as built does not collect the reward, for the reason in its own §3. The contraction is delivered by running plug at w_eff = 2.1-3.7 mean (gpu#15, up to +10.4 per step) aimed at a shifted target, so it moves bias by up to 1.8 delta along the ladder and MAE/delta degrades monotonically in 5 of 6 blocks (gpu#11) — the opposite sign to the -21/-32% the clean lever predicts. And every e4t0.5 cell fails the chemistry floor on alpha and gap (§6.2). My +0.0295 counterfactual is the ceiling of a *clean* spread intervention, and at BDG's own n=512 it is z = +1.46 to +1.62 — below the project's z>=3 bar. So the defensible claim is: the lever is real, is priced into the project's own metrics, and is 7-8x the centring lever at a median target; BDG demonstrates monotone requested-to-achieved control of it (6/6, two seeds, replicated at B=256 by gpu#7); what is *not* demonstrated is collecting the metric gain at fixed centring and fixed chemistry. That is one experiment, not a redesign.

CAVEAT ON MY OWN EVIDENCE: items (1), (2) and (6)'s counterfactuals are rescorings of 15,000 real samples — data, not simulation. Items (4)'s batch-size numbers come from the calibrated mean-field loop with a homogeneous gain and a Gaussian batch; the real sampler has heterogeneous |J^T g|^2 and kurtosis 2.4-6.4 (math#13), which would raise between-batch variance somewhat. That is why E1 below is a real-sampler check and costs 8 minutes.

If (b) fails — if BDG reaches the same spread at materially better chemistry — that is the first genuine result in the method and belongs in the paper's §4.4.

Deliberately NOT proposed: any q90 or dist BDG run, any n=5000x3 run, and any entry into the tuned chain (different delta, freeze_tune.py refuses a mixed tree). The q90 and dist verdicts are already settled against BDG by the counterfactuals above and need no compute.

R3 — §1, replace the first two sentences and add the target scope (this is the load-bearing change):

Every guidance arm nevertheless optimises a *centring* objective and exposes one knob that moves centring and spread together. BDG adds a feedback loop on the spread. **It works** — monotone requested-to-achieved on 6/6 curves across two seeds, `sd/unguided` 0.65 to 1.17. **We do not show that it collects the metric gain**, and §3 says why: the contraction is delivered at an effective weight `w_eff` of 2-4x aimed at a shifted target, so it moves the centre too and breaks the chemistry floor. State the target in every table."

R4 — delete "widening lowers coverage by definition" from §1 and §6.2 and replace with "widening lowers coverage whenever `|bias| <~ delta`, which is the q50 regime; at q90 the optimum spread ratio is 1.10-1.40 and widening raises coverage by +0.001 to +0.005."

ruling.rationale:
I re-ran the defence's d5_q50_reward.py, d6_mae_lever.py and d1_batch_modes.py and got the quoted numbers exactly. I also checked its repo citations: ARM_RANKINGS.md:8, :22-24 and :33-35, FR3A_VS_FR3_COMPARISON.md:243, evaluation.py:311-320 and BDG_HANDOFF.md:181-182 all say what the defence says.

WHERE THE DEFENCE WINS
(1) The objection's wording "no project metric rewards spread" is too absolute, and it is false.
- At q50, contracting real unguided residuals to the spread ratio BDG achieved raises in_band by +0.0295/+0.0225/+0.0296 (mu/alpha/gap). Perfect centring buys only +0.0036/-0.0018/+0.0045.
- MAE/delta falls 21-32% at q50 and 2-8% at q90.
- "spread" is already a named column in ARM_RANKINGS.md.
(2) At B=1 the dispersion term multiplies F_i - F_bar = 0, so BDG in its spec form is exactly plug. So BDG has no single-molecule capability, but it does not fail either. It needs a guard, because an unguarded V_b is 0/0 = NaN. This point barely matters anyway: no cell in the repo runs below B=128.
(3) Nothing measured supports "cannot be matched without changing the method" (doable#18 item 5). Running 4 controllers of 128 does not change the per-step rule.

WHERE THE OBJECTION STANDS
(a) The project's headline verdict is decided on in_band at q90 (FULL_RUN_V2_PROTOCOL.md V7). The protocol chose q90 over q50 on purpose (lines 78-81: "the median leaves almost nothing to show").
- At q90, tightening to BDG's ratios LOWERS in_band by -0.0056/-0.0103/-0.0304 (reproduced).
- Widening buys at most +0.005.
- Debiasing buys +0.024 to +0.051.
- The defence concedes all of this.
(b) What the q50 metrics reward is contraction, not setpoint control. Plug's strength knob already collects that reward: plug w=4 on gap scores 0.1602 in_band, against BDG e4t0.5's 0.1523. So BDG's distinctive capability (a requested setpoint, and widening) earns nothing on any verdict metric. Widening strictly lowers in_band at q50 (D5b is monotone on 3/3 properties).
(c) The MAE result is not evidence for BDG. E|b + s*d| is convex in s, and its slope at s=0 is sign(b)*E[d] = 0, so MAE falls under contraction for ANY residual distribution, any arm and any target. "Monotone on 6/6" is guaranteed by the maths, not found in the data. The same applies to the q50 in_band gain when |bias| is small next to delta.
(d) Even the ceiling of a clean spread intervention is z = +1.46 to +1.62 at n=512, below the project's z>=3 bar. BDG as built also moves bias by up to 1.8 delta (gpu#11). The defence concedes this in its item 6.
(e) The dist sub-claim, the diversity sub-claim and the missing distribution-matching metric are all conceded, and all are correct.

ON BATCH = n
The evidence against the handoff's batch==n rule comes only from a model, a homogeneous-gain Gaussian loop. I reproduced it: 4x128 vs 1x512 moves pooled sd by at most 0.16%. But that model's fitted gain (kappa about 1e-3) does not match the real controller. Measured w_eff flips sign up to 34 times per window and ranges from -2.6 to +10.4 (gpu#12, gpu#15). math#18 also flagged the model as inconsistent with the handoff's own frozen-weight control. At B=128 the estimator noise is twice as large, which matters most near w_eff about 0 (math#15). So the rule "batch == n" is unproven as a necessity, but R1's "compatible" and "preferable" are equally unproven until E1 runs. Batch size is also only 1 of the 10 protocol mismatches in doable#18. Fixing it does not let BDG into the v2 or tuned headline tables, so "the protocol conflict becomes a footnote" overreaches.

Net result: the headline wording and the B=1 point are refuted, and batch==n is open. But the substance holds at the project's own verdict target: no headline metric rewards BDG's spread CONTROL, and the q50 reward for contraction is one an existing arm already collects.
