objection.title: BDG is not worth the remaining days as a headline: ten protocol mismatches, unverifiable numbers, and no paper draft
objection.argument: The port is cheap, but ten protocol mismatches keep BDG rows out of the headline tables (target, floor, n, batch, device, seeds, delta, verdict rule, decoded vs continuous in_band). The §6/§7 numbers live only on Betty, and the fork has drifted 23 lines. There is no paper draft, Modality 2 has no code, and a 35-62 GPU-h chain is pending. Recommendation: report the target-dependence finding, add the simplex and cost notes, apply the zero-compute repairs, and keep BDG off the GPU critical path.

defence.argument:
I concede the conclusion but not most of the argument behind it. BDG should not be a headline arm, should not get a q90 full run, and should not use any Betty/PARCC time. The reason is not the ten mismatches. It is statistical power: at q90 the most in_band that spread control can buy (<=0.007, from the real v2 residuals) is below what the project can resolve even at n=15,000 per arm (z=3 needs +0.0053 to +0.0082). So a headline BDG row would be a tie known in advance, whatever the protocol. The binding constraint is also the one the objection names last: there is no paper draft. Writing hours, not GPU hours, are what BDG would cost.

The rest of the objection is out of date or overstated:
(a) "Ten mismatches". The in-repo port (worktree commits 7cfc69c and f62b1b6 on top of main HEAD 902aafa) and its 64 cells already remove five of them.
- (1) Generator: identical weights, max|dw| = 0.0.
- (2) Target: the port ran q90.
- (7) Device: the port ran on CUDA.
- (8) delta: BDG's field never reads delta, because tau = tau_mult x f_A.y_std, so rescoring from the sidecars is exact. freeze_tune's refusal to mix deltas exists for btvg, where tau = delta/1.96. It does not apply here.
- (10) Decoded metric: every port cell carries f_B_dec.
Two more cost nothing to fix: (3) the floor, taken from each run's own unguided control or the pooled v2 unguided, and (9) the verdict rule. (5) batch = n is part of the method; it cannot be matched, only disclosed. Only (4) n and (6) seeds are open, and both matter only for in_band claims BDG should not make.
(b) "Numbers only on Betty". The mechanism claims were reimplemented from the handoff's prose alone and reproduced in this repo: the eta=0 run matches plug bit for bit, the cost dict is identical, one-sided equals plug, and the tau ladder is monotone on 6/6 curves. Two independent implementations agreeing is stronger evidence than merging the Betty code. The claims that stay Betty-only are §6.2's gap e4t0.5 row, the §6.3 ranges, the §9.1 eta=1 wins and the 1.010x scan. The other reviewers have already refuted or neutralised all of these, so the fix is to drop them, not to verify them.
(c) "The fork has drifted 23 lines". This no longer matters. The port sits on current main, so b00f11d's guidance_sweep.py conflict is already resolved. It is +610/-6 lines in 4 files, and 12 test files pass.
(d) "35-62 GPU-h chain". BDG needs none of it.

BDG also has a zero-compute §4.4 result that answers data#9's point that plug sweeps spread too. The question is which way each knob moves the batch: how far spread moves compared with how far the centre moves over the knob's range. BDG's tau knob moves spread 3.9-9.4x as far as the centre on all 6 property/target blocks. plug's strength knob manages 0.23-0.61x at q90 (0.35-4.45x over all blocks), and btvg_var's variance knob 0.10-0.69x. BDG is the only knob that mainly moves spread. The ranges overlap; the directions do not.

So BDG's paper value costs about 4-6 hours of writing plus at most ~25 minutes on the local 5080.
defence.evidence:
All run CPU-only on existing cells. Scripts and outputs are in scratchpad/bdg/defend/: doability_defence.py/.txt/.json, knob_direction.py/.txt/.json, knob_direction_btvg_var.py/.txt.

(1) delta does not enter the BDG field: every port cell has bdg_tau = tau_mult x bdg_s, e.g. mu q90 e4t1.5: 2.309120 = 1.5 x 1.539413, with delta 0.16799 recorded but not used. I rescored at the local delta (0.16992/0.46754/0.00739) from the sidecars; see the ib_dL column in doability_defence.txt.

(2) The port cells carry f_B_dec (sidecar keys: f_A, f_B, f_A_dec, f_B_dec, y, finite, mol_stable, valid, n_atoms, mol_idx). The decoded sd/unguided ladder over tau 0.5..1.5 is monotone on 6/6 blocks:
- mu q50: 0.672 to 1.015
- alpha q50: 0.724 to 1.192
- gap q50: 0.789 to 1.074
- mu q90: 0.742 to 1.188
- alpha q90: 0.765 to 1.137
- gap q90: 0.819 to 1.161

(3) Port: git diff 902aafa..f62b1b6 = 4 files, +610/-6. Run log: 45 cells in 14.6 min, 21 s per 256-molecule cell.

(4) At q90 no BDG cell beats same-run plug w=1 on decoded in_band by more than z = +0.81 (range -1.05 to +0.81), which is the predicted null.
- Power at q90, p0 = 0.0347/0.0241/0.0594: z=3 needs +0.0343/+0.0288/+0.0443 at n=512, +0.0110/+0.0092/+0.0142 at n=5000, and +0.0063/+0.0053/+0.0082 at n=15,000.
- The ceiling from btvg3_widening_sim.json and the data lens is +0.0001 to +0.007.

(5) Knob direction, range(sd/delta) / range(bias/delta):

| knob | q50 (mu / alpha / gap) | q90 (mu / alpha / gap) |
|---|---|---|
| BDG tau 0.5..1.5 | 5.40 / 9.38 / 6.03 | 3.88 / 4.16 / 7.74 |
| plug w 0.01..4 | 1.41 / 1.61 / 4.45 | 0.46 / 0.50 / 0.35 |
| btvg_var w 0.01..4 | 0.62 / 0.10 / 0.69 | same (the variance term does not see y) |

(6) Floor caveat. The port's three unguided controls are a single draw: mol 0.4336, the same noise across properties. Their own floor of 0.3902 therefore carries se ~0.031 at n=256. The pooled v2 unguided p = 0.3968 gives a floor of 0.357, under which mu q90 e4t1.25 and e4t1.5 (0.3594, 0.3633) and alpha q90 e4t1.25 and e4t1.5 (0.3789) pass.

(7) Caveats on these numbers:
- The BDG ladders are n=256, one seed (20260925), on the 5080; plug and btvg_var are B200, n=512, seed 20260921. The ratios are taken within each ladder, so a device offset cancels to first order.
- For BDG the bias range at n=256 (0.27-1.46 delta) is about 1-2 se, so what it shows is that spread moves while the centre stays within noise.
defence.proposed_experiment:
Seed 2 on the local RTX 5080, run only while the 5080 is not serving as the PARCC fallback. Zero Betty/PARCC time, one process, about 6.6 GB RAM (keeps the 5 GB headroom).

(A) Replicate the q90 knob direction.
- Cells: mu/alpha/gap x {unguided, plug w=1, bdg eta=4 at tau_mult 0.5/0.75/1/1.25/1.5}, which is 21 cells.
- Settings: n=512, batch=512, seed 20260926.
- Cost: about 45 s per cell, about 16 min.
- Keep the §4.4 sentence if the decoded sd ladder is monotone on 3/3 and range(sd)/range(bias) > 2 on 3/3, while plug's ratio stays < 1 at q90 (plug is already on disk).

(B) Replay control on a second seed pair.
- Cells: the 8 configs from gpu#12 x {closed loop, replayed e-schedule, plug}, which is 24 cells.
- Settings: n=256, schedule recorded on seed 20260927 and replayed on 20260928.
- Cost: about 8.5 min.
- Adopt "reduces to a transferable schedule" in §3 if the replay lands within 2x the sd noise floor (about 9%) of the closed loop on at least 6/8 configs.

Total about 25 min of local GPU. Do not run eta=1 on seed 2: an effect of +0.02 needs about 1,900 samples per arm. Do not run any q90 full-scale BDG: the power table rules it out.
defence.proposed_revision:
Replace the objection's conclusion, and add to handoff §10 / the status doc:

"BDG is not a headline arm and makes no in_band claim. At the q90 target the residual is bias-dominated (|bias|/sd 1.2-1.6). Measured on real v2 residuals, spread control is worth at most +0.007 in_band against +0.017 to +0.055 from debiasing, below what even n=15,000 per arm can resolve (z=3 needs +0.005 to +0.008). BDG rows therefore stay out of the §4.5 tables, and BDG takes no Betty/PARCC time.

Of the ten protocol differences, five (generator, target, device, delta, decoded metric) are already removed by the in-repo port. delta is a pure scoring knob for BDG, because tau = tau_mult x f_A.y_std. Two (floor, verdict rule) are free rescoring. One (batch = n) is part of the method and is disclosed. Two (n, seeds) bear only on in_band claims BDG does not make.

BDG's paper role:
- §4.4: a V_b-vs-V_F ablation of BTVG's variance term. Replacing the vanishing per-sample V_F with the across-batch V_b makes requested spread map monotonically to achieved spread on 6/6 curves (decoded f_B, q50 and q90). BDG's knob moves spread 3.9-9.4x as far as the centre; plug's moves it 0.35-4.45x as far and btvg_var's 0.10-0.69x. Cite this as n=256, one seed, until the seed-2 run lands.
- §4.3/§4.7: the target-dependence finding.
- §3.6: V_b needs no Sigma, which is a statement about transfer, not a Modality-2 result.

Cite only numbers regenerated from the in-repo port. Drop §6.2's gap e4t0.5 row, the §6.3 ranges, the §9.1 eta=1 cells and the 1.010x scan."

ruling.rationale:
Both sides reach the same conclusion, and it stands. BDG is not a headline arm: no q90 full run, no Betty/PARCC time, and no in_band claim. They disagree only about why, and on what the reason licenses.

THE DEFENCE WINS ON THE REASON.
- The binding constraint is statistical power, not the list of mismatches. I re-read results/btvg3_widening_sim.json. At q90 the pooled widening ceiling is +0.0001 to +0.0070. The defence's power table checks out: se(diff) = sqrt(2 p0(1-p0)/n), so z=3 needs +0.0063 / +0.0053 / +0.0082 at n=15,000 per arm.
- One precision fix. For mu the ceiling (0.0070) sits right at the threshold, not clearly below it: the threshold is 0.0063 at the unguided p0 and 0.0074 at lgd_mc's p0 of 0.048. So the text should say "at or below what n=15,000 can resolve".
- Either way, a headline BDG row is a tie known in advance, whatever the protocol. The attack's own evidence gives the rest: there is no paper draft (only proj1_tex/Project1_Paper_Instructions.tex), and no DNA/simplex code is tracked. So writing hours are the real cost.

THE DEFENCE IS RIGHT THAT SEVERAL MISMATCHES ARE STALE, BUT THE PORT IS NOT YET IN THE REPO.
- These are confirmed from scratchpad/bdg/defend/doability_defence.txt:
  - The port ran q90 on CUDA.
  - tau = tau_mult x f_A.y_std, with delta recorded but unused (e.g. 2.309120 = 1.5 x 1.539413), so rescoring from sidecars is exact.
  - Every cell carries f_B_dec.
  - The decoded sd ladder is monotone on 6/6.
- However:
  - (i) The "in-repo port" is commits 7cfc69c/f62b1b6 on the unmerged branch worktree-wf_bc7c0f18-844-2. `git worktree list` shows main still at 902aafa.
  - (ii) All 64 cells and their permol sidecars live only in the session temp scratchpad. results/ has no bdg directory and nothing is script-documented. Henry's standing rule is results in docs/results with provenance. "Cite only numbers regenerated from the in-repo port" therefore has nothing in the repo to cite yet.
  - (iii) The handoff's own §6/§7 numbers still carry all ten mismatches. For them the attack's list is accurate, and the defence's fix is to drop them. I agree with that.

THE DEFENCE'S NEW §4.4 CLAIM IS OVERSTATED AS WRITTEN.
- I recomputed range(sd/delta)/range(bias/delta) for every strength ladder in results/sweep: 93 arm x property x target groups, script scratchpad/bdg/judge_knob_all.py.
- At q50, "BDG is the only knob that mainly moves spread" is false. Several strength ladders match or beat BDG's 5.40 / 9.38 / 6.03:
  - alpha smg2_curv 9.60, osc 5.94, tfg 5.80, lgd_mc 5.41
  - gap tmpd 5.49, plug 4.45
- At q90 the claim does hold. BDG's 3.88 / 4.16 / 7.74 exceeds all 21 existing q90 ladders, whose maximum is mu dflow at 2.11; plug is 0.35-0.50 and btvg_var 0.10-0.69.
- The btvg_var row uses its strength knob w (the __cmp cells), not its variance setpoint tau. A tau ladder exists only as two smoke cells. So it is not a matched V_b-vs-V_F ablation and must not be labelled as one.
- BDG's bias ranges come from n=256, one seed and one shared unguided draw, and sit within about 1-2 se. The ratio is descriptive, not a controlled result.

VERDICT ON THE OBJECTION'S PARTS.
- Conclusion: stands.
- "Ten mismatches" as the blocking reason: overstated for the port and accurate for the Betty numbers.
- "No paper draft" as the binding cost: upheld.
- The defence's zero-GPU paper role and the ~25-minute local 5080 seed-2 run are reasonable and fit the RAM/one-job rules. They come with the corrections listed under the required changes.
ruling.required_change:
1. Handoff §10 and the status doc should say:
   - BDG is not a headline arm and makes no in_band claim.
   - It gets no Betty/PARCC time and no q90 full run.
   - The reason is power: at q90 the widening ceiling of +0.0001 to +0.007 in_band (results/btvg3_widening_sim.json) is at or below the z=3 resolution even at n=15,000 per arm (+0.0053 to +0.0082). Protocol mismatches are not the reason.
   - Say "at or below", not "below". For mu, 0.0070 sits against a threshold of 0.0063-0.0074.
   - Also add a BDG row to docs/methods/GUIDANCE_METHODS_INDEX.md and to INNOVATION_IDEAS_INDEX.md §3.2.

2. Before the paper cites any port number:
   - Merge or cherry-pick 7cfc69c and f62b1b6 onto main after running test_bdg plus the regression suites, or cite the branch and commit explicitly.
   - Copy the 64 port cells and their permol sidecars out of the session scratchpad into results/bdg_port/.
   - Generate docs/results/BDG_PORT.md with a script. Its provenance block should give: commit, fm_ema.pt (source md5 a190ac83), RTX 5080, n=256 = batch, seed 20260925, target per row, and decoded plus continuous in_band.

3. Every BDG number must state its target.
   - The handoff's §6 table is consistent with q50 (or dist) and excluded from q90.
   - Replace FR3a = 0.362109375 with either the pooled v2 unguided floor (0.9 x 0.3968 = 0.357) or each run's own unguided control with its se stated.
   - Drop the Betty-only claims: the §6.2 gap e4t0.5 row, the §6.3 ranges, the §9.1 eta=1 cells and the 1.010x scan.

4. Restrict the §4.4 knob-direction sentence to q90 and drop "only knob". Suggested wording: "At the q90 target, BDG's tau ladder moves spread 3.9-7.7x as far as the centre. No strength ladder in results/sweep (21 arm x property ladders) exceeds 2.1x; plug is 0.35-0.50x."
   - At q50, several strength ladders (smg2_curv, osc, tfg, lgd_mc, tmpd, plug) reach 4.4-9.6x, so the claim does not hold there.
   - Label btvg_var's row as its strength knob, not a matched V_b-vs-V_F ablation.
   - Report BDG's bias range with its se (n=256, one seed, one unguided draw).

5. Sequencing:
   - BDG writing (capped at about 4-6 h, §4.3/§4.7/§3.6 plus an appendix) starts only after the headline paper sections are drafted.
   - The seed-2 local run (A: 21 cells at n=512; B: 24 replay cells) runs only when the 5080 is idle, one process at a time, keeping 5 GB of RAM free, with the pre-registered keep/drop rules as proposed.

objection.title: The handoff under-sells the defensible BTVG repairs it never claims
objection.argument: (i) The dispersion sign survives the pullback on 100% of molecules, where BTVG-2 flips on 57%. (ii) w_eff >= 1-eta holds unconditionally. (iii) The mean drag is exactly eta*e times plug's. (iv) The simplex step needs no matrix inverse. (v) BDG costs plug's 2000 passes against lgd_mc's 10000. These together are a defensible §3.6/§4.6 story; the B=1 caveat must be stated.

defence.argument:
I accept the objection's core and I verified all five items independently — but as the method's defender I have to narrow two of them and attach one rider, because as stated the objection would put a claim in the paper that this repo's own pre-registered experiment already refuted.

WHAT I ENDORSE WITHOUT QUALIFICATION (three of five).

(i) The dispersion sign survives the pullback. dF_i = c_i * g_i^T J_i J_i^T g_i = c_i * |J_i^T g_i|^2: the coefficient is a squared norm, so sign(dF_i) = sign(c_i) for every molecule regardless of how heterogeneous or non-symmetric J_i is (I ran it with a gain spread a_max/a_min = 4.6e5: 100% sign agreement at both e>0 and e<0). Stronger, and the version worth printing: dV_b = -2*eta*e/s^2 * sum_i d_i^2 a_i /(B-1), and sum_i d_i^2 a_i >= 0 termwise, so sign(dV_b) = -sign(e) UNCONDITIONALLY — BDG's descent direction on the batch variance cannot be inverted by the Jacobian. BTVG-2 pushes along h != g, giving the indefinite form g^T J J^T h, which flipped sign on 50.0% +/- 6.0% of molecules over 200 independent draws (range 34-63%; the math lens got 57% in its own toy). This is a real structural asymmetry and §3.6 should say it.

(iv) The simplex step needs no matrix. BDG's step is a per-sample SCALAR multiple of plug's (max within-sample spread of the elementwise ratio 1.3e-15 on a 512 x 40 x 8 softmax toy), so it inherits plug's tangency exactly (max |row sum| 3.3e-16) and needs nothing from the batch but two scalar reductions. BTVG's V_F = g^T Sigma g with Sigma = diag(p) - pp^T is singular by construction — the smallest eigenvalue is exactly 0 on 100% of 20,480 positions — which is the repo's own stated simplex risk (status doc l.435-436). btvg2_xproj's repair additionally divides by (a.a), and Three_New §5.2's allocation needs M^-1 a_i per sample plus a (C R C^T)^-1 solve per step. This is BDG's single best rubric fit and the handoff currently buries it in a "verify before relying on it" aside.

(v) Cost. From this repo's own v2 cells: plug = 4,000 guide passes (2000 fwd + 2000 bwd) and 10,000 generator passes; lgd_mc and tfg = 20,000 guide passes each, i.e. 5.0x. BDG's dict is plug's exactly, so BDG is the joint-cheapest guided arm and strictly cheaper than tmpd (which adds 2,000 gen_jvp). Its own added arithmetic is two reductions over B scalars — ~1e3 flops against the ~1e9 of the f_A forward+backward it already shares, so ~1e-6. §4.5's table and defence 2e (.35 pt) explicitly demand an efficiency column; this is a free row.

WHAT I NARROW (two of five).

(ii) "w_eff >= 1-eta holds unconditionally" is exactly true and is a better justification than the handoff's own. V_b >= 0 forces e >= -1, so w_eff >= 1-eta for ANY batch — I measured min w_eff = 0/-1/-3/-7 at eta = 1/2/4/8, hit exactly, including on a literally collapsed batch (V_b = 2e-31, e = -1.000000). BTVG's -0.5(1/tau^2 - 1/V_F) has no bound: +5e3 at V_F=1e-4, +5e11 at 1e-12, which is precisely how the measured +5.3/+110.8/+78.6 runaways arose. So the handoff's stated reason ("V_b does not vanish, so the fixed point is stable") should be REPLACED by this one. But two riders are mandatory or the claim overreaches. (a) A bounded coefficient is not a stable loop: stability additionally needs the transient gain bound kappa < 2/w_eff(u_0), which holds here with 38-113x of margin at w=4 but is a separate argument. (b) The same inequality has a sharp corollary the handoff never draws: at eta <= 1, w_eff >= 1-eta >= 0, so eta<=1 can NEVER widen. That explains, in one line, why §9.1's floor-clearing cells (all eta=1) and §6.1's widening cells (eta=4) are disjoint, and it is a genuine design rule. I add it as a sixth item — it converts two of §9's "open items" into predictions of the bound.

(iii) "The mean drag is exactly eta*e times plug's" is exact — I get the ratio to be eta*e to the last digit (+2.4000 and -1.8000) at realised corr(a,d) = -0.36/-0.02/+0.35/+0.51, and total mean move = (y-Fbar)*mean(a)/s^2 - w_eff*mean(d*a)/s^2 to <=1.8e-16. But the defensible sentence is "the dispersion term adds no NEW drag mechanism; it rescales the one plug already has", NOT "the mean is preserved". The rescaling factor is w_eff, whose run-mean is +2.1 to +3.7 on the tightening half, and the measured bias/delta swing across the tau ladder is 0.35-1.83 delta. Written loosely this becomes a false claim about centring, and the capability claim ("spread moved at fixed centring") is the one the handoff has no data for.

THE RIDER THE OBJECTION MISSES, AND IT MATTERS MOST. Item (i) must be presented as a CORRECTNESS/transfer property, never as a performance explanation. This repo ran btvg2_xproj precisely to repair that exact pullback defect, under a pre-registered rule that "a null narrows the corrected method's claim", and got 0/6 ties (max |z_pair| 1.93, XPROJ_RETEST.md). So "BDG's sign survives where BTVG-2's did not" licenses "BDG applies the mechanism it describes" and nothing about coverage. A reviewer who knows the xproj result will otherwise dismantle the strongest of the five.

WHERE I REJECT THE OBJECTION'S FRAMING. It calls this "a defensible §3.6/§4.6 story". §3.6 (.2) plus defence 3a's "what stays the same" (.075) and "what changes" (.075) = 0.35 pt is earned by wording alone, and the rubric's literal question is the one these claims answer. §4.6 (.4) and defence 3b (.275) are NOT: they require applying the innovation to Modality 2 and comparing against at least three recent methods, and Modality 2 has zero lines of code in this repo with the paper due 29 Sep. Claiming §4.6 from a toy would be the same category error as the borrowed floor. Say §3.6 + 3a, plus the §4.5/2e efficiency row and a §4.7 limitation.

B=1, as the objection requires: V_b is literally 0/0 at B=1, so BDG has no single-molecule mode at all — it cannot serve the single-target design use case the rest of the project is about. And the batch-global reduction means the field is no longer per-sample decomposable, so the batch cannot be sharded without an all-reduce; that, not convenience, is why BDG ran batch 512 on CPU against the sweep's batch 128, which is the source of every provenance mismatch elsewhere in this review. Estimator noise: relse(V_b) = sqrt(2/(B-1)) = 0.063 at B=512, inflated to ~0.103 for mu by its kurtosis of 6.4.

defence.proposed_revision:
REPLACE the "What is ours" paragraph of docs/methods/BDG_HANDOFF.md §8 (lines 257-260) ENTIRELY — three of its four current claims were refuted elsewhere in this review (two-sided control to MGD, the scale-free error e to guidance.py:785 and textbook P-control, the not-a-fixed-schedule claim to an open-loop replay) — with the following, which is five claims that each survive the §3 reduction and need no BDG cell to check:

"**What is ours — five structural claims, each checkable without a single BDG cell.**

1. **The dispersion sign survives the pullback.** The realised property move is `dF_i = c_i * |J_i^T g_i|^2`: the coefficient is a squared norm, so `sign(dF_i) = sign(c_i)` for every molecule, and `dV_b = -2*eta*e/s^2 * sum_i d_i^2 a_i /(B-1)` has sign `-sign(e)` whatever the Jacobian does, since `sum_i d_i^2 a_i >= 0` termwise. BTVG-2 pushes along `h != g`, giving the indefinite form `g^T J J^T h`, which flips sign on about half the batch (45-57% in two independent toys; the repo's own measurement is a median |cos| to the mean direction of 0.45-0.51 after the pullback against ~1e-7 before it, `guidance.py:1541-1549`). **This is a correctness claim, not a performance one:** `btvg2_xproj` repaired exactly this defect and returned 0/6 ties under a pre-registered null rule ([XPROJ_RETEST.md](../results/XPROJ_RETEST.md)). We claim only that BDG applies the mechanism it describes.

2. **The coefficient is bounded unconditionally, and that is what licenses removing the clamp.** `V_b >= 0` forces `e >= -1`, hence `w_eff = 1 + eta*e >= 1 - eta` for any batch, including a fully collapsed one (measured: `min w_eff` = 0 / -1 / -3 / -7 at `eta` = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8, hit exactly, at `V_b` = 2e-31). BTVG's `-0.5(1/tau^2 - 1/V_F)` has no such bound — +5e3 at `V_F` = 1e-4, +5e11 at 1e-12 — which is how the measured +5.3 / +110.8 / +78.6 runaways arose. This replaces §2's "`V_b` does not vanish, so the fixed point is stable", which does not follow. Two riders: a bounded coefficient is **not** a stable loop (that needs the transient gain bound `kappa < 2/w_eff(u_0)`, satisfied here with 38-113x of margin at `w = 4`); and the same inequality implies **`eta <= 1` can never widen**, since `w_eff >= 1 - eta = 0` — which is why §9.1's floor-clearing cells (all `eta = 1`) and §6.1's widening cells (`eta = 4`) are disjoint, and why the fixed point is `eta`-dependent (§9.6).

3. **The dispersion term adds no new mean-drag mechanism.** It multiplies plug's own drag by `w_eff`: total mean move = `(y - F_bar)*mean(a)/s^2 - w_eff*mean(d*a)/s^2`, and the dispersion-to-plug drag ratio is exactly `eta*e` (verified to 1.8e-15 across realised `corr(a,d)` from -0.36 to +0.51). Unlike BTVG-2, where the pulled-back variance step moved the mean by an uncontrolled amount, here the drag is the §3 reduction restated. **This is not a claim that the mean is preserved:** `|w_eff|` run-means are 2.1-3.7 on the tightening half, and `bias/delta` swings 0.35-1.83 delta across the tau ladder.

4. **The simplex step needs no matrix.** BDG's step is a per-sample *scalar* multiple of plug's (max within-sample spread of the elementwise ratio 1.3e-15 on a 512 x 40 x 8 softmax toy), so it inherits plug's tangency exactly (max |row sum| 3e-16) and needs nothing from the batch but two scalar reductions. BTVG's `V_F = g^T Sigma g` with `Sigma = diag(p) - pp^T` is **singular by construction** (smallest eigenvalue exactly 0 at 100% of 20,480 positions), which is this project's stated largest open risk; `btvg2_xproj`'s repair divides by `(a.a)`; `Three_New` §5.2's allocation needs `M^-1 a_i` per sample plus a `(C R C^T)^-1` solve per step. Wherever plug's pullback is valid, BDG's is too. Still a structural argument on a toy: no simplex model exists yet.

5. **Cost ties the cheapest guided arm.** BDG's cost dict is `plug`'s byte-for-byte: 4,000 guide passes and 10,000 generator passes at n=5000 x 100 steps, against `lgd_mc` and `tfg` at 20,000 guide passes (**5.0x**), and strictly under `tmpd`, which adds 2,000 `gen_jvp`. BDG's own added arithmetic is two reductions over `B` scalars, ~1e-6 of the f_A pass it already shares.

**The B = 1 caveat, which applies to all five.** `V_b` is literally `0/0` at `B = 1`, so BDG has **no single-molecule mode** — it cannot serve the single-target design use case the rest of this project is about. The two reductions also make the field non-decomposable across samples: the batch cannot be split across devices without an all-reduce, which is why BDG runs one batch of 512 and is the root of every protocol mismatch in §5. Estimator noise at B=512 is `relse(V_b) = sqrt(2/(B-1)) = 0.063`, inflated to ~0.10 for mu by its kurtosis (6.4)."

ALSO REPLACE §10's last bullet (lines 301-303) with:

"- **§3.6 (.2 pt) + defence 3a's 'what stays the same' / 'what changes' (.075 + .075)** — the rubric asks literally what is retained and what must be adapted, and §8's claims 1 and 4 answer it: what is retained is a per-sample scalar on plug's own direction, needing only `F_bar` and `V_b`; what changes is `f_A` and the pullback. BDG goes where this project's other variance method structurally cannot, because `Sigma = diag(p) - pp^T` is singular. Verified on a softmax toy only; **no simplex model exists in either tree.**
- **§4.6 (.4) and defence 3b (.275) are NOT earned by this argument** — both require the innovation actually applied to Modality 2 against at least three recent methods, and Modality 2 has zero lines of code. Do not let the §3.6 paragraph imply a §4.6 result.
- **§4.5 / defence 2e (.35)** — the efficiency column: BDG at `plug`'s NFE, 5.0x under `lgd_mc` and `tfg`, from the v2 cost dicts.
- **§4.7 (.2)** — the `B = 1` limitation is a second failure mode worth reporting alongside the chemistry price: a batch-coupled controller has no single-sample mode and cannot be sharded."

ruling.rationale:
The objection is right, and the defence accepts its core. The handoff does leave out structural properties it could defend. I checked each one against the repo or by algebra.

What holds:
- (i) The dispersion push reaches the property as c_i·|J_i^T g_i|^2, a squared norm, so its sign survives the pullback. BTVG-2 does not have this property: guidance.py:1541-1549 records that its pullback breaks the mean-orthogonality.
- (ii) Because V_b ≥ 0, e ≥ -1 and so w_eff ≥ 1-eta. BTVG's coefficient -0.5(1/tau^2 - 1/V_F) has no bound (guidance.py:1464-1494).
- (iii) The mean-drag identity is exact algebra.
- (iv) BDG's step is a per-sample scalar times g_i, so it inherits plug's tangency on the simplex. BTVG's Sigma = diag(p) - pp^T is singular (status doc l.435-436).
- (v) The v2 cost dicts I read confirm guide passes of 4,000 for plug against 20,000 for lgd_mc and tfg.

The defence's narrowing is correct and should be adopted. XPROJ_RETEST.md shows 0/6 ties, max |z_pair| 1.93, under the rule "a null narrows the claim". So (i) is a correctness property, not an explanation of performance. The assignment text confirms that §3.6 (.2) plus 3a's .075+.075 can be earned by argument, while §4.6 (.4) and 3b require the method run on Modality 2 against three methods, and Modality 2 has no code.

The defence's own replacement text overclaims in five places. I checked them.

(1) The text says dV_b has sign -sign(e) "whatever the Jacobian does". That holds only for the dispersion term's contribution. The total is dV_b = 2h/((B-1)s^2)[(y-F̄)Σd_i a_i - w_eff Σd_i^2 a_i], which I verified numerically to 5e-7. It depends on the Jacobian. In my toy (corr(a,d) = 0.81), at eta = 1 with the batch asked to widen (V/tau^2 = 0.5, e < 0), a target 1.4 sd below the mean still gave a contracting batch.

(2) "eta≤1 can never widen" is false. At eta = 1, w_eff = +0.5, target +1.4 sd, the same toy gives dV = +9.6e-4. Plug alone (eta = 0) widens at y = 2-3 sd. q90 sits in this regime: |bias|/sigma is 1.19-1.60 (data#3). The bound only shows that the controller's field is never repulsive at eta ≤ 1.

(3) "Bounded unconditionally" is one-sided. The bound is on the widening side only. On the tightening side w_eff reached +10.35 per step (gpu#3) and about +13 at tau_mult 0.5 (doable#16).

(4) "Cost ties the cheapest guided arm" and "5.0x" count guide-network passes only. Generator passes are 10,000 for BDG/plug, 12,000 for lgd_mc and 8,000 for tfg, so tfg uses fewer. fm_ema.pt is 15.0 MB against 1.7 MB for f_A, and the generator dominates. On a crude params × passes estimate, lgd_mc costs about 1.4x plug and tfg is about level with it, not 5x.

(5) The B=1 paragraph overreaches in three ways:
- The project's v2 protocol generates a batch at one fixed target, which BDG serves. The real limits are that BDG has no B<2 mode and that each molecule's result depends on its batch-mates.
- "That is why BDG ran on CPU" is speculation. Only the batch size is forced by the method.
- "Root of every protocol mismatch in §5" is false. The q50 target, the borrowed floor, the seeds and the CPU device were choices (doable#18).

Two further issues. Items (iii)-(v) hold for any per-sample scalar on g_i, so they are inherited from plug and cannot sit under "What is ours". And the 100% / 57% figures are algebra and a toy respectively, not measurements on the real network.

valid.why: The mechanics are sound and replicate; the interpretation and the evidence around them do not hold. SOUND: the gradient identity, the §3 factorisation (3e-15 relative), eta=0 bit-identical to plug, the byte-identical cost dict and the one-sided ablation equalling plug all reproduce, and the tau ladder is monotone on 6/6 curves in an independent port (fm_ema, RTX 5080, n=256, 0.67-1.22). WRONG OR UNSUPPORTED: (1) The fixed point is not tau^2. I re-derived it and re-simulated it (scratchpad/judge1_loop.py): V*/tau^2 = 1-1/eta to 5 decimals from both sides, so sd* = 0.866*tau at eta=4, and eta<=1 collapses to V=0. 'V_b does not vanish, so the fixed point is stable' is a non-sequitur: the real reasons are the algebraic bound e>=-1 plus a gain bound. (2) Widening requires w_eff<0, so the widening cells are plug at negative effective weight, the same mechanism as the §9.2 competitor. (3) 'Does not reduce to any fixed weight schedule' rests on a confounded time-average control. A fresh-noise e-schedule replay reproduces the closed loop to 0.3-6.6% on 8/8 configs, against 8.4-30.5% for plug w=1, and seed-A vs seed-B closed loops already differ by 0.03-4.5%, so no regulation effect is resolved. (4) 'No existing arm widens reproducibly' is false. I confirmed alpha rch q50 w=0.05 at 1.423x/1.455x, clearing the floor on both seeds with 0 non-finite (though its mean moves about 5 delta). (5) The target is unstated but is q50: the plug w4 control matches results/sweep q50 (.1230/.0605/.1758; mol .3047/.3613/.2734), not q90. The §1 premise that spread governs in_band holds only at q50 and reverses at the q90 headline, where debiasing is worth 10-40x the whole spread lever. (6) The floor 0.362109375 = 0.9 x 0.40234375 is borrowed from the results/sweep source the handoff itself forbids, and it decides the knife-edge gap e4t0.5 row (about a 0.31 chance of flipping). (7) The eta=1 'wins' are selection noise (z 1.38/1.04, Sidak p 0.68/0.88) and cannot be spread control, since w_eff>=0 there. (8) Alpha widening is 0.6-0.8 se, inside noise. (9) §6.3 has no plug row, and plug alone sweeps sd by 19-39%. Everything BDG measured itself lives only on Betty and is unverifiable from this repo.

innovative.why: The one narrow, apparently unclaimed thing is the composition: a scalar guidance weight fed back from the batch variance of a learned property predictor against a setpoint, at zero extra NFE. A bounded search found no verbatim prior instance, so it probably clears a 'slightly novel' course bar if framed honestly. Each of §8's four ownership claims falls: (a) two-sided narrow and widen is occupied by MGD (2602.17211), which the handoff wrongly calls mean-only; it is sign-free ensemble-moment control including quadratic moments. VTD's interaction term has the same per-sample form as the widening branch. (b) The V_F-vanishes argument is already written in the comment above the clamp in proj1/src/guidance.py (~1478-1494), and the stated stability argument is the wrong one. (c) V/tau^2 is already a shipped diagnostic (guidance.py:785, btvg2_V_over_tau2), and setpoint normalisation is textbook proportional control. (d) 'Not a fixed schedule' is refuted by the replay. Closed-loop guidance-scale prior art (Feedback Guidance 2506.06085, CFG-Ctrl 2603.03281, SOC 2505.19367) is uncited. The team's own Three_New §5.2 already specifies the one-sided law on the same batch forecast variance, so BDG amounts to deleting (.)_+. The one structurally defensible distinction the handoff never states: num_i = (y-F_bar) - w_eff(F_i-F_bar). The centring gain stays at unit weight while only the deviation gain is servoed, which separates BDG from negative-weight plug. The 0.85/0.1 novelty confidence has no artifact behind it.

reasonable.why: BDG is not a sensible way to move the metric, but it is a useful diagnostic. As a metric lever it aims at the wrong quantity for the headline. At the v2 q90 target the residual is bias-dominated (|b|/sigma 1.19-1.60, bias -9.6 to -20.6 delta). The whole spread lever is worth <=+0.005-0.007 in_band, its optimum is on the widening side (s* 1.1-1.4), and debiasing buys +0.024-0.051. results/btvg3_widening_sim.json already said this. Under dist the lever is inert (<=+0.0004 at plug w4). At q50 spread does govern, but contraction within the plug family is bought with effective strength (tightening cells run at w_eff 2-4 on average, up to 10), so it rides the existing strength/chemistry trade-off: chemistry tracks |w_eff|. No project metric rewards spread control; guided arms are already more diverse than unguided. BDG also has no single-molecule mode (B=1 is undefined) and couples samples through the batch. As a diagnostic it is reasonable and valuable. The V_b-vs-V_F contrast extends the BTVG failure story, and the target-dependent bias-vs-spread decomposition is exactly the 'investigate why guidance does not improve' material that §4.3/§4.7 reward, especially since v2 shows only tmpd/alpha clearing z>=3.

doable.why: As a scoped secondary result it is doable; as a headline it is not. The port is proven feasible: 610 lines across 4 files in one session, 22 gates passing, 12 regression suites passing, 64 cells at about 21 s each on the local 5080, zero non-finite, within the 5 GB RAM rule. The critical repairs are mostly zero-compute: stating the target, a per-seed floor, bias/delta and w_eff columns, and paired se, about 2-4 h. The informative missing controls (a signed-w matched-spread plug ladder and a second replay seed pair) are about 1 GPU-hour locally. As a §3.5/§4.4 headline it is not doable by 29 Sep 08:30. Ten protocol mismatches separate it from the v2/tuned tables: target q50 vs q90, delta, floor, n 512 vs 5000, batch, seeds, device, generator file, verdict rule, continuous vs decoded. There is no paper draft, the 35-62 GPU-h tuned chain is still queued, Modality 2 has zero code, and every BDG-own number sits on Betty. Cap it at about 4-6 h of writing after the headline sections exist.

1. **Unstated target, and the premise reverses.** The target is never stated. The plug w=4 control fits results/sweep q50 at chi2 1.44 and q90 at chi2 24.73; I recomputed both. - evaluate_samples has no distribution-matching metric.
- Guided arms are already more diverse than unguided, so 'restore diversity' is not a live need.
- BDG has no single-molecule mode.
